korean: 이번엔 이름만 보고 정한 거 아냐.
before: This time I didn't decide just by a name.
after: This time I didn't choose on the strength of a name alone.

before: It gets louder when I speak in a hurry.
after: My voice gets louder when I speak in a hurry.

korean: 말하기 힘든 옛 이름은 안 물을게요. 남기고 싶은 말부터 해요.
before: I won't ask an old name that's hard to say. Start with what you want remembered.
after: I won't make you say the old name if it's hard. Start with what you want remembered.

korean: 지금 이름을 아껴도 잃어버린 얘기는 하고 싶어.
before: Even cherishing my name now, I want to talk about what I lost.
after: I value the name I have now, but I still want to talk about what I lost.

korean: 오늘 함께 한 일과 집안 얘기를 나눠 봐요.
before: Let's separate today's work together from your family history.
after: Let's talk about today's work together without confusing it with your family history.

before: You won't cover it all with saying we're the same.
after: You won't brush it all aside by saying we're the same.

korean: 그렇다고 매번 못 들은 척하면 안 되지.
before: That doesn't mean we can pretend I never heard, every time.
after: That doesn't mean we should keep excusing me for not listening.

korean: 지쳤다는 말도 무리 안에서 해도 되는 말이겠지.
before: Being tired should be something I can say within the group, too.
after: I should be able to tell the group I'm tired, too.

korean: 앞장서던 날처럼 오늘은 늦게 온 사람을 기다릴게.
before: Like on the days I led, today I'll wait for whoever comes late.
after: I've taken the lead before. Today I'll wait for whoever comes late.

korean: 부탁으로 연 문은 같이 나가고 싶어.
before: I opened this door with a request. I'd like to go through together.
after: I asked you to join me when I opened the door. I'd like us to go through together.

before: Me changing doesn't make the load lighter.
after: Changing my ways doesn't make the load lighter.

korean: 같이 드는 손이 무거울 때만 있으면 아쉽잖아.
before: It'd be sad if there were only helping hands for heavy loads.
after: It'd be sad if people only helped each other with heavy loads.

before: This name is what's become comfortable.
after: I've grown comfortable with this name.

korean: 지금은 내 말보다 그 사람 말을 들어.
before: Right now, hear them rather than me.
after: Right now, listen to them rather than me.

korean: 다 못 지켰어도 다시 사람부터 보자.
before: Even if we couldn't protect everything, let's look to people first again.
after: Even if we couldn't protect everything, let's put people first again.

before: You took even the words I should choose.
after: You even chose my words for me.

before: You looked for a use before a name.
after: You thought of a use for me before asking my name.

before: Please ask them yourselves.
after: Please ask them yourself.

korean: 직접 확인하면 제 말 때문에 헷갈리진 않겠어요.
before: Checking yourself should keep my words from confusing things.
after: Checking for yourself should keep my words from muddling things.

korean: 제 이름이 붙으면 없던 신뢰도 생겨요.
before: Put my name on it and you create trust that wasn't there.
after: Use my name and it'll sound as though I've vouched for it.

korean: 닫기 전에 갈 거면 길에서 확인해 봐요.
before: If you're going before closing, check on the way.
after: Check their hours on the way, so you don't arrive after closing.

before: Let's look at the situation before choosing together.
after: Let's consider the situation together before choosing a phrase.

before: I've some amusing gossip.
after: I've got some amusing gossip.

korean: 나중에 다른 분한테 제가 한 말까지 의심받고요.
before: Later, other people will doubt even things I've actually told them.
after: Then people might doubt even the things I really did say.

korean: 제가 말 꼬인 얘기도 꽤 많아요.
before: I've plenty of stories about stumbling over my own words.
after: I've got plenty of stories about stumbling over my own words.

before: On the island, the time after hello was long.
after: On the island, the silence after a greeting felt very long.

korean: 제 것을 받았다고 주문을 넣고 싶진 않아요.
before: Getting mine doesn't make me want to place orders.
after: Just because I received one doesn't mean I want to start placing orders.

korean: 물 마실 동안은 저도 말 좀 아낄래요.
before: While we drink, I'll spare my words a little too.
after: While we drink, I'll talk a little less, too.

korean: 그냥 없던 일로 하긴 싫어서 말했어요.
before: I told you because I didn't want to just let it disappear.
after: I told you because I didn't want to let our plans fall through without a word.

korean: 모르는 데 가면 괜히 손해 볼 텐데요.
before: An unfamiliar place might be a waste.
after: Trying somewhere unfamiliar might be a waste.

before: I'll take it slowly from the middle.
after: I'll take my time picking up where we left off.

korean: 어디부터 걸을지 저도 처음부터 같이 생각해요.
before: I'll think about where to start with you from the beginning, too.
after: I'll choose where to start our walk with you, too.

before: I'll tell you the streets of Torva when we're back.
after: I'll tell you about the streets of Torva when we're back.

before: We'll choose what to eat after returning when we're back.
after: We'll choose where to eat once we're back.

before: Tell me if my voice speeds up.
after: Tell me if I start speaking too quickly.

before: Telling this fight's story will take a while later.
after: It'll take a while to tell the story of this fight later.

before: We'll hear you're fine after we've checked!
after: You can tell me you're fine after we've checked!

korean: 쉬는 동안엔 제 입도 좀 쉴게요.
before: While we rest, I'll rest my mouth, too.
after: While we rest, I'll take a break from talking, too.

before: For now, stop your hands before following your curiosity.
after: For now, keep your hands back, however curious you are.

korean: 안 들은 말로 달래 주려는 건가?
before: Soothing me with something you haven't even heard?
after: Trying to reassure me before you've even heard me out?

before: Warming up my mouth.
after: Just warming up my voice.

before: Add just to that and even asking becomes difficult.
after: When you say 'just,' even asking becomes difficult.

korean: 다 맞는다는 말은 제가 해도 못 믿겠는데요.
before: I wouldn't believe everything was fine even if I said it.
after: Even if I said I was fine, I wouldn't believe it myself.

before: Nice to need fewer words before it.
after: Nice to be able to say it without so much preamble.

korean: 웃는 얼굴까지 만들어 보이기는 좀 피곤하네.
before: Making a smiling face is rather tiring as well.
after: Even forcing a smile gets tiring.

korean: 내가 못 막았다는 말이 자꾸 남아서요.
before: The words I couldn't stop it keep staying with me.
after: The words 'I couldn't stop it' keep coming back to me.

korean: 부적을 쥐어도 그날 답까지 생기진 않아요.
before: Holding the charm doesn't answer that day for me.
after: Holding the charm doesn't give me an answer about that day.

korean: 없던 일로 하면 서로 뭐가 남죠?
before: Erase them, and what do either of us have left?
after: Erase them, and what does either of us have left?

before: You took those words before the object.
after: You listened to what I said before taking the charm.

korean: 나 대신 겁을 끝내려 하진 말아요.
before: Don't try to finish my fear for me.
after: Don't try to resolve my fear for me.

before: As long as I don't only hear about them behind my back.
after: As long as I don't have to find out after you've changed them behind my back.

korean: 묻기로 한 다음부터도 이번만은 계속 나올 수 있죠.
before: Even after agreeing to ask, just this once can keep coming.
after: Even after a promise to ask, 'just this once' keeps coming back.

korean: 없을 거라는 답은 아직 못 들을 것 같아요.
before: I don't think I can hear that nothing will happen yet.
after: I'm not ready to hear that nothing will happen.

before: I wasn’t just making small talk.
after: That wasn't just idle chatter.

korean: 입 푸는 중이니 먼저 가지 마요.
before: I'm warming up my mouth. Don't go ahead.
after: I'm warming up my voice. Don't go ahead.

before: I told you, I'm warming up my mouth before shooting.
after: I told you, I'm warming up my voice before shooting.

before: Coming back together is still ahead of us.
after: We still have to make it back together.

before: Call their name first. Decide the conclusion later.
after: Call their name first. Draw conclusions later.

before: There are still things our hands can do before wishing.
after: There's still something we can do before resorting to wishes.

korean: 오늘은 입 푸는 것도 쉬고 싶어요.
before: Today I'd like a rest even from warming up my mouth.
after: Today I'd like a break even from warming up my voice.

before: I'd like room for a quiet face, too.
after: I'd like room to be quiet, too.

before: Before scolding whoever couldn't keep up.
after: Do that before scolding whoever couldn't keep up.

before: If knowing only what I saw is enough.
after: That is, if you're willing to hear only what I saw.

before: Let's look again at just this once first.
after: Let's look again at this 'just this once' first.

before: This time I'm not warming up my mouth.
after: This time I'm not warming up my voice.

korean: 남의 장비에 흠집 내고 할 말은 아니다.
before: Not something to say after scratching someone else's equipment.
after: That is no excuse for scratching someone else's equipment.

korean: 오래 쓴 것이라 더 함부로 놓고 싶지 않다.
before: Having used it so long makes me less willing to leave it carelessly.
after: I have used it too long to leave it lying carelessly.

korean: 그럼 그 말은 받겠다. 그, 잘 봤군.
before: Then I accept. You, ah, noticed well.
after: Then I accept. You, ah, were paying attention.

before: She fiddles with her cup at the recognition of her efforts.
after: She fiddles with her cup when you acknowledge her efforts.

before: If your praise comes from seeing it, I accept.
after: If you are praising what you actually saw, I accept.

before: The von remained.
after: The 'von' remained.

korean: 폰까지 적은 이유를 오늘은 말해 봤다.
before: Today I spoke of why I wrote the von, too.
after: Today I also explained why I wrote the 'von.'

korean: 그걸 보고 자꾸 물으면 더 꼬여.
before: Keep questioning it and I get more tangled.
after: Keep asking about it and I stumble over my words even more.

before: I was making a noise, touching it so much.
after: I was making a noise, fiddling with it so much.

before: I only raised my voice for nothing.
after: I raised my voice for no reason.

before: I'll join you on the name of Halen.
after: I'll join you in the name of Halen.

korean: 같이 있고 싶다는 말엔 가문을 안 붙였다.
before: I left my family name out of asking for your company.
after: I asked for your company without invoking my family name.

korean: 약속 때문에 숨기는 건 더 싫다.
before: I would dislike you hiding it for the promise even more.
after: I would dislike it even more if you hid your difficulty for the sake of the promise.

korean: 적은 뒤에 서로 한 번 더 보자.
before: Once written, let us both review it again.
after: Once the tasks are written down, let us both review them again.

before: Let's cover the mistake for your family's sake.
after: Let's cover up the mistake for your family's sake.

korean: 의자 앞에서 내 지시만 기다리게 하긴 싫었다.
before: I did not want you waiting before a chair for instructions alone.
after: I did not want you standing before a chair waiting to be told to sit.

before: You need not write them as the correct answer.
after: You need not present them as the only correct answer.

before: Tell me when you’re ready to leave.
after: Tell me when you are ready to leave.

before: I watch the front. Cover the rear!
after: I will watch the front. Cover the rear!

before: I will not invoke my name to overreach.
after: I will not invoke my name to demand more than we can do.

korean: 이름을 댈 힘보다 쉴 힘을 남겨라.
before: Save your strength for rest rather than proclaiming your name.
after: Rest and save your strength instead of proclaiming your name.

korean: 앉은 뒤엔 바로 지시부터 내리지 않겠다.
before: Once seated, I will not start with instructions at once.
after: Once seated, I will not immediately start giving instructions.

before: I understand a welcome without my name.
after: I can understand a welcome even without hearing my name.

before: You would recognize even just Gunhild.
after: You would recognize me even as just Gunhild.

korean: 펼친 문서에서 확인할 줄만 남겨 두었소.
before: I have left only the lines to check on the open document.
after: I have left the document open only at the lines we need to check.

korean: 내가 읽은 문장도 그 결정에 들어가야 하오.
before: The words I read must be part of that decision, too.
after: The wording I have read must inform that decision, too.

before: Shall we compare it beside the wording before signing?
after: Shall we compare it with the wording we signed?

before: I will postpone performance while you check.
after: I will wait to carry out the agreement while you check.

korean: 좋은 뜻도 함께 읽어야 같은 약속이 되오.
before: Even good intentions must be read together to make the same promise.
after: Even with good intentions, we must read it together to agree on the same promise.

korean: 같이 들은 뜻이 있어야 다음에 이행하오.
before: I can fulfill it next time only with a meaning we have both heard.
after: I can fulfill it next time only if we both understand its meaning.

korean: 바뀐 글씨 옆에는 아직 제 확인이 없소.
before: My confirmation is not beside the amended writing yet.
after: I have not yet confirmed the amended wording.

before: It is a name that stands as surety.
after: The name itself serves as a guarantee.

before: A name of surety is not writing to shorten.
after: A name pledged as a guarantee must not be shortened.

korean: 그림자 없는 쪽에서 한 줄 더 읽겠소.
before: I will read another line out of the shadow.
after: I will read another line here, out of the shadows.

korean: 밖에서 났어도 자꾸 귀가 그쪽으로 가오.
before: Even outside, it keeps drawing my ears.
after: Even if it came from outside, I keep listening for it.

korean: 문을 한번 확인하면 다음 글자도 보이겠소.
before: One check of the door should let me see the next letter.
after: Once I have checked the door, I should be able to read on.

before: Even my hands had drawn back.
after: I see I had even pulled my hands back.

korean: 덜 지킬 수 있는 몫도 내 혼자 고를 수는 없소.
before: I cannot choose alone which obligations to fulfill less.
after: I cannot decide by myself which obligations to leave partly unfulfilled.

korean: 추가하지 않은 품도 제 손이 고른 일이오.
before: Even unrecorded work was a choice made by my own hands.
after: Even without a record, helping was my own choice.

before: Watching behind made my explanation longer.
after: I kept looking behind me and taking longer to explain.

before: The name of surety was heavy even on days I upheld it.
after: The name I pledged weighed on me even when I upheld it.

before: I could read the letters, but the meaning would not enter.
after: I could read the words, but I could not take in their meaning.

korean: 지금 곁에 있어 달라는 말은 늦었구려.
before: I was late in asking you to stay beside me now.
after: I should have asked sooner for you to stay beside me now.

before: Saying it aloud makes this side clearer.
after: Saying it aloud makes what is here feel clearer.

korean: 안 적어도 지킨다는 말을 제가 기억할게요.
before: I'll remember your promise to keep it unwritten, too.
after: I'll remember that you said you would keep the promise even without writing it down.

before: Even your presence will tell me.
after: I will know you are there even by the sound of your movements.

before: This time I spoke to ask for a person.
after: This time I spoke because I wanted someone's company.

korean: 그래도 뒤에 남은 사람 수에 나도 넣으시오.
before: Still, count me among those left behind.
after: Still, count me among those who might fall behind.

korean: 믿는다는 말로 묻는 일을 없애고 싶지 않소.
before: I do not want trust to remove the asking.
after: I do not want trust to mean we stop asking.

korean: 오늘 확인한 말에는 침묵의 서명이 없소.
before: There is no silent signature on the words confirmed today.
after: We did not take silence as a signature on the promise we confirmed today.

korean: 끝난 의뢰 밖에서 기다릴 시간을 골랐소.
before: Outside the finished commission, I chose time to wait.
after: The commission was over, but I chose to spend my own time waiting.

before: Then I will close the paper.
after: Then I will put the document away.

before: The document is closed. Will you listen a moment?
after: I have put the document away. Will you listen a moment?

before: Haldric writes out the guarantor’s full name.
after: Haldric writes out the full name pledged as a guarantee.

before: You did not clear a document's width as well.
after: You did not leave extra space for a document, either.

korean: 오늘은 제가 늦지 않게 옆에 올게요.
before: Today I'll come beside you without being late.
after: Today I'll join you without keeping you waiting.

korean: 당연한 일에도 내 말은 남기고 싶소.
before: Even for something natural, I want my own words to remain.
after: Even when it seems natural, I want to say it in my own words.

korean: 번호 없이 고맙다고 말하는 일이 오늘은 덜 어렵소.
before: Today, thanking you without a number is less difficult.
after: Today it is easier to thank you without first reciting an article number.

before: Even leaving the document, I remember the promise.
after: Even without the document, I remember the promise.

before: Read the unfavorable shares without omitting them, too.
after: Read out the unfavorable terms too, without omitting them.

before: Today's kept promises included staying beside someone.
after: Staying beside someone was among the promises we kept today.

before: I must hear that claim of enduring alone again.
after: I need to question that claim that you can endure it alone.

before: If you need help, use my side too.
after: If you need help, call on me as well.

before: I will wait here together, too.
after: I will wait here with you, too.

before: Today I will borrow a hand.
after: Today I will ask for help.

before: I will rest together a little before going.
after: I will rest with you a little before going.

before: Even unable to open it, our promise to return is unchanged.
after: Even if we cannot open it, our promise to return is unchanged.

before: Check the completed scope first.
after: Check how much of the agreed work is complete first.

korean: 들은 뒤에 고르겠소. 아직 서명할 뜻은 아니오.
before: I will choose afterward. This is not yet an intention to sign.
after: I will choose afterward. Hearing you out does not mean I intend to sign.

before: I do not yet know the line you changed first.
after: I do not yet know which line you changed without asking.

before: You read a willing act as a condition.
after: You took a voluntary act as one of the terms.

before: Today I will align our agreed duties first.
after: Today I will make sure we agree on our duties first.

before: I thought it would be the same unwritten.
after: I thought we would understand it the same way even without writing it down.

before: I will make no promises amended through silence.
after: I will not let silence amend our promises.

before: That order makes it difficult to call this agreement.
after: Signing before reading makes it difficult to call this an agreement.

korean: 직접 적는 일까지 덜어 낼 생각은 없습니다.
before: I do not intend to spare myself the writing, too.
after: I do not intend to avoid the work of writing it myself.

before: I am writing a name to call it.
after: I am choosing what to call it.

korean: 그 이름으로 불러야 제가 덜 망설입니다.
before: That name lets me call it with less hesitation.
after: Using that name helps me cast it with less hesitation.

korean: 작성자를 건너뛰면 작은 글자도 다르게 남습니다.
before: Bypassing the author changes how even a small letter remains.
after: Even a small change leaves a different record if the author has no say.

before: I write until we return to Lumiel.
after: I write, 'Until we return to Lumiel.'

korean: 그 이름이 제 판단까지 대신하진 않습니다.
before: That label does not judge in my place.
after: That label cannot make my judgment for me.

before: I will not begrudge it for revisions.
after: I will use as much as I need for revisions.

korean: 그냥 쉬자는 말을 끝까지 하고 싶었습니다.
before: I wanted to finish simply asking to rest.
after: I wanted simply to ask to rest, and leave it at that.

korean: 혼자 정한 문장에 서명만 받진 않겠습니다.
before: I will not decide a sentence alone and only ask your signature.
after: I will not decide the wording alone and merely ask for your signature.

korean: 다른 말이 나오면 처음부터 다시 맞추겠습니다.
before: If we differ, we will align it again from the beginning.
after: If we disagree, we will work through the wording again from the beginning.

korean: 그럼 다음엔 제 부탁부터 들어 주세요.
before: Then hear my favor first next time.
after: Then agree to my next request before hearing it.

before: I will wet my throat before explaining.
after: I will take a sip of water before explaining.

before: I will speak tomorrow's greeting now.
after: I will say aloud now that I would like to see you tomorrow.

before: I will check companions before making a record.
after: I will check on our companions before making a record.

before: During this time, I will wet my throat first.
after: For now, I will have something to drink first.

before: I have confirmed a seal. Stop your hands.
after: I have confirmed it is sealed. Keep your hands back.

before: I’ll say my remaining goodbyes aloud.
after: I will say the rest of my goodbyes aloud.

before: I would like you to hear those meanings separately.
after: I would like you to distinguish the name from the effect.

korean: 등은 제 눈으로 살피기 어렵습니다. 확인하겠습니다.
before: My back is difficult to inspect myself. I will check.
after: It is difficult to inspect my own back. I will check.

before: Knight's armor must hold up well on its own.
after: A knight's armor must hold up well on its own.

korean: 멈추라는 말도 따르겠습니다. 앞에서 안 보이는 것은 부탁드려야 합니다.
before: I will stop if asked. I must rely on you for what I cannot see ahead.
after: I will stop if asked. I must rely on you for what I cannot see behind me.

korean: 제가 먹는 동안은 부탁드리겠습니다. 한 숟갈쯤 늦어도 괜찮겠습니다.
before: Then I entrust that to you while I eat. A spoonful's delay should be all right.
after: Then I entrust that to you while I eat. Surely I can take a spoonful before looking again.

korean: 닫아 버리면 더 궁금할 것 같습니다. 제가 좀 우습지 않습니까?
before: Closing it would only make me more curious. Rather ridiculous, am I not?
after: Closing it would only make me more curious. I am rather ridiculous, am I not?

korean: 돌아간 뒤의 일부터 정하면 여기 남은 마음은 또 말하지 못할 것 같습니다.
before: If we decide what happens after I return first, I may never explain why I want to stay.
after: If we start deciding what I will do after returning, I may never explain why I want to stay.

korean: 잠깐 같이 있어 달라는 부탁이었는데, 제가 너무 빙 돌렸습니다.
before: I was asking you to stay a moment. I made it far too roundabout.
after: I was asking you to stay a moment. I took far too long to say it plainly.

korean: 괜찮다고 해 버리면 또 말하지 못할 것 같습니다. 이번에는 교대를 부탁드립니다.
before: If I say I am fine, I may never say it. This time I ask to be relieved.
after: If I say I am fine, I may never ask. This time, I am asking to be relieved.

korean: 오늘 좋았다는 말은 좀 늦게 해도 전해지겠습니까? 저도 이제 해 보겠습니다.
before: Will it still mean something if I am late saying today was good? Let me try now.
after: Is it too late to say I am glad about today? I would like to say it now.

korean: 제 의견도 한번 멈춰 세워 주십시오.
before: Please stop my proposals for a moment too.
after: Please ask me to pause and reconsider my proposals, too.

korean: 차를 기다리는 동안은 아무 일도 정하지 않겠습니다.
before: While we wait for tea, I will decide no duties.
after: While we wait for tea, I will not assign any duties.

korean: 져도 같이 돌아갑니다. 제 손이 필요한 분 계십니까?
before: Even if we lose, we’ll return together. Does anyone need help?
after: Even if we lose, we will return together. Does anyone need help?

before: I would ask about your role in the next expedition.
after: I would like to ask about your role in the next expedition.

before: There were things I overlooked, assuming they were fine.
after: There were things I overlooked because I assumed they were fine.

before: A relaxed talk might change your mind.
after: A relaxed conversation might change your mind.

korean: 제 판단은 분위기 때문에 바뀌지 않습니다.
before: Atmosphere does not change my judgment.
after: A pleasant atmosphere does not change my judgment.

before: Freshly drawn. Still cold.
after: It was freshly drawn. It is still cold.

korean: 이쪽은 조금 비켜 앉는 편이 좋겠습니다.
before: Better to sit a little farther aside.
after: I had better move my chair a little to the side.

before: I will move back a moment.
after: I will move back a little.

before: Halfway is enough.
after: Drawing it halfway will be enough.

before: It should not delay us much.
after: It should not take much longer.

before: So it’s all right to forget if we don’t write it down.
after: So it is all right to forget if we do not write it down.

korean: 남겨 두면 다른 날 쓸 수 있습니다.
before: Saved, they can serve another day.
after: If I keep them, I can use them another day.

before: I do not know if the water prompted it.
after: I do not know whether the water brought it to mind.

before: That way should have been less crowded now.
after: That way should have been less crowded at this hour.

before: Ready at the agreed time.
after: I am ready at the agreed time.

before: We will examine where our views differ together.
after: We will examine our different observations together.

before: You may say if you think it too much.
after: You may say if you think it is too much.

before: If you need my hand, I will offer it at once.
after: If you need help, I will offer it at once.

before: Can you move your hand first?
after: First, can you move your hand?

before: I will check my movement immediately.
after: I will check how well I can move immediately.

korean: 오늘은 제 판단을 잠깐 봐 주십시오.
before: Today, please watch my judgment a moment too.
after: Today, please keep an eye on my decisions, too.

before: I need help on my side too.
after: I need help as well.

before: This is the water we drank in Tarn Valley.
after: This reminds me of the water we drank in Tarn Valley.

before: So even protection can have grasping hands.
after: So you can take control of my work in the name of protection, too.

korean: 덮은 계산을 동의한 계산으로 읽진 마세요.
before: Don't read covered calculations as consent.
after: Covered calculations aren't an invitation to read them.

before: No permission?
after: Because I had no permission?

korean: 제가 하는 일보다 허가한 이름을 먼저 보시네요.
before: You look for the name approving it before looking at my work.
after: You look for an approving signature before looking at my work.

before: A question that considers my skill.
after: A question about what I can do.

before: What differed first?
after: Where did the first difference appear?

korean: 모르는 부분을 알게 되는 데 시간이 더 걸려요.
before: Finding out what you don't know takes even longer.
after: It takes even longer to figure out which details you don't know.

korean: 원인은 제가 고를 테니…… 아니, 함께 봐요.
before: I'll choose the cause... No, let's examine it together.
after: I'll decide the cause... No, let's examine it together.

before: All right. Starting with my own work.
after: All right. Let me start with my own work.

korean: 남의 답을 들을 때는 제 펜도 조금 늦춰야겠어요.
before: My pen needs to slow down when others answer too.
after: My pen needs to slow down while I listen to answers, too.

korean: 불을 옮길 수 있는데 연구부터 접네요.
before: You abandon the research when we could move the flame.
after: You'd set aside the research when we could just move the flame.

korean: 이 사람들까지 생각하면 간단히 정할 순 없겠네요.
before: Considering these people makes it hard to decide simply.
after: It's harder to make a simple decision when you consider these people.

korean: 모르는 걸 범인 얘기로 채우지 않으시네요.
before: You aren't filling ignorance with accusations.
after: You aren't filling the gaps in what you know with accusations.

korean: 싫은 표정을 못 읽으면 좋은 방법도 소용없죠.
before: Even a good method is useless if I can't recognize her refusal.
after: Even a good method is useless if I won't listen when she refuses.

korean: 큰 발견이 아깝네요. 다음엔 혼자라도 가요.
before: What a lost discovery. Go alone next time if necessary.
after: What a discovery to miss. Go alone next time if you have to.

korean: 오늘 감사는 다음 계획의 대가로 안 적겠어요.
before: I won't record today's thanks as payment for the next plan.
after: My thanks today aren't payment for helping with the next plan.

korean: 못 풀어도 같이 본 데까지는 남는군요.
before: Even unsolved, the part we examined together remains.
after: Even without a solution, we still have what we examined together.

korean: 모르는 칸 앞에서도 같이 있을 수 있네요.
before: We can stay together before an unanswered space too.
after: We can stay together even in front of an unsolved problem.

before: So no promise to review it together.
after: So you won't promise to review it with me.

korean: 처음엔 왜 몰랐는지 알아야 다음에 덜 틀려요.
before: Knowing why I missed it first means fewer mistakes next time.
after: Knowing why I missed it in the first place means fewer mistakes next time.

korean: 못 푼 채로도 같이 앉아 있고 싶었어요.
before: I wanted to sit together with it still unsolved.
after: I wanted to sit together even with the problem unsolved.

korean: 빨리 가자는 말은 조금 늦게 할게요.
before: I'll delay saying we should hurry a little.
after: I'll wait a little before telling everyone to hurry.

korean: 제 생각이 빠르면 한번 세워 주세요.
before: Stop my thoughts a moment if they race ahead.
after: Ask me to pause if my thoughts race ahead.

before: I won't calculate without the people following.
after: I won't leave the people following out of my calculations.

before: Hands first now. Counting mistakes can wait.
after: Help them first. Counting mistakes can wait.

korean: 도움이 필요한 건 아는 것과 달라요.
before: Needing help is different from knowing things.
after: Knowing what to do doesn't mean I don't need help.

before: Clever people can hurt too.
after: Even clever people get hurt.

korean: 못 연 걸 혼자 부끄러워하진 않을게요.
before: I won't bear the shame of not opening it alone.
after: I won't be the only one ashamed that we couldn't open it.

before: I wasn't just seeking an agreeable face.
after: I wasn't just looking for someone to nod along.

before: About when I was expelled.
after: About the time I was expelled...

before: Even near the answer, I could come back.
after: Even with the answer so close, I was able to turn back.

korean: 누굴 보고 한 말인지 다시 들을게요.
before: I'll listen again to whom those words concerned.
after: I'll listen again to who those words were about.

before: Leave it while I am briefly away.
after: Please leave the choice to me, even if I am away for a moment.

before: Less gloomy for eating too.
after: It is less gloomy here for eating, too.

korean: 같은 뜻인 줄 알고 읽다가 멈췄어요.
before: I stopped after assuming the wording meant the same.
after: I had to stop after assuming the wording meant the same thing.

korean: 같은 뜻인지 확인할 곳이 한 군데 남았어요.
before: One passage remains to check for the same meaning.
after: I still need to check whether one passage means the same thing.

before: Hopefully, nothing too complicated.
after: I hope it is not too complicated.

korean: 저 골목에서는 구운 냄새가 오래 나네요.
before: The smell of roasting lingers in that alley.
after: The smell of roasted food lingers in that alley.

korean: 몇 해 지냈는데도 남은 버릇이 있어요.
before: Years, yet some habits remain.
after: I have been here for years, but some habits remain.

korean: 그때는 질문처럼 들리게 말해 보고 싶어요.
before: I want it to sound like a question when I do.
after: I want her to hear it as a question when I ask.

before: Yes. Spoon first.
after: Yes. I will pick up my spoon first.

korean: 손을 펴고 있으니 종이 넘기던 힘이 빠지네요.
before: Opening my hands eases the tension from turning pages.
after: Keeping my hands open eases the tension from turning pages.

korean: 예. 방금 나온 것이 뭔지 궁금해요.
before: Yes. I wonder what just came out.
after: Yes. I wonder what the kitchen has just served.

korean: 조금 떨리지만 확인은 할 수 있어요.
before: A little nervous, but I can still check.
after: I am a little nervous, but I can still check.

before: My strength is leaving all at once.
after: All at once, I feel drained.

before: You are before me. I will reach out first.
after: You are right here. I will reach out to help you first.

before: Water first, briefly.
after: I will just have some water first.

before: I won’t pretend I don’t see that feeling, either.
after: I will not pretend I do not feel that wish to help, either.

korean: 아직 못 나가겠다는 답도 잠깐 남겨 주세요.
before: Let my answer that I can't go out stand a moment too.
after: Please let my answer stand for a moment. I can't go out yet.

before: Bear it a little. You'll warm up. I do.
after: Bear it a little. You'll warm up. I always do.

before: But it seems a little short.
after: But I don't think it's quite enough.

korean: 참다가 너무 늦게 말씀드릴까 봐 걱정됐어요.
before: I worried that enduring it would make me speak too late.
after: I worried that if I kept bearing it, I'd speak up too late.

korean: 크기부터 줄이지 말고 어디 아픈지 들려주세요.
before: Don't make it smaller first. Tell me where it hurts.
after: Don't play it down first. Tell me where it hurts.

korean: 아무것도 안 묻는 건 아닌 것 같아서요.
before: I don't think it means she never wonders.
after: I don't think being quiet means she has no questions.

korean: 문을 지나면 돌아갈 수 없을까 봐 망설였어요.
before: I hesitated, afraid crossing the door meant I could never return.
after: I hesitated, afraid that going through the door meant I could never return.

korean: 쓰겠다고 해도 멈출 말은 남겨 두고 싶어요.
before: Even when I agree, I want the words to stop left available.
after: Even when I agree to use my power, I still want to be able to ask to stop.

before: I meant us to choose together next.
after: I thought we could choose our cups together this time.

korean: 두 잔을 놓은 뒤에는 둘이 골라도 되겠죠?
before: With two cups out, the two of us may choose, right?
after: With two cups out, we can both choose, right?

before: I'd like to share a cup with you.
after: I'd like to have some with you.

korean: 오늘 괜찮은 만큼만 말해도 다 들리네요.
before: Saying only what's better today can still be heard fully.
after: You hear me out even when I only say how much better I feel today.

before: Would you have tea in the same seats?
after: Would you have tea with me in the same seats?

korean: 할 수 있다고 해도 멈출 말은 남겨요.
before: Even if I can, leave me the words to stop.
after: Even if I can do it, let me ask to stop.

korean: 전부 괜찮은 건 아니어도 같이 기뻐요.
before: Not everything is fine, but I'm glad with you.
after: Not everything is fine, but I'm happy we can celebrate together.

korean: 제가 한 몫도 같이 보실 건가요?
before: Will you consider my contribution too?
after: Will you recognize what I did to help, too?

korean: 누가 먼저인지 정하기 전에 이름을 불러요.
before: Call their names before deciding who comes first.
after: Call their names before deciding whom to check first.

korean: 못 열어도 제가 잘못했다고 먼저 말하진 않아요.
before: Even if it won't open, I won't begin by saying I did wrong.
after: Even if it won't open, I won't start by blaming myself.

before: You asked me closer a little too soon.
after: You asked me to come closer a little too soon.

korean: 먹을 수 없는 걸 많이 받아도 곤란해요.
before: Plenty they can't eat would be troublesome.
after: A large amount of something they can't eat would be troublesome.

before: Good for tracing the letters.
after: It will be good for going over the letters.

korean: 제 밥까지 마음대로 나누진 말아 주세요.
before: Please don't give my dinner away without asking too.
after: Please don't give my dinner away without asking, either.

before: Served it late, but it's still good.
after: I served it late, but it is still good.

korean: 아니라고 듣고 싶어서 묻는 건 맞아요.
before: Yes, I'm asking because I want to hear no.
after: I admit I'm hoping you'll say they won't.

korean: 누가 못 먹었을까 봐 들은 걸 또 묻게 돼요.
before: Fear someone went hungry makes me ask again.
after: I'm afraid someone went hungry. That's why I keep asking.

korean: 그분이 돌아가시며 이 책을 제게 맡기셨어요.
before: At their death, they entrusted this book to me.
after: They entrusted this book to me as they were dying.

before: How did opening it first feel?
after: How did you feel when you first opened the book?

before: Then, I thought of it as the book I received.
after: At the time, I thought of it as the book entrusted to me.

before: I nearly cooled the bowl searching again.
after: I nearly let the food go cold searching for it again.

before: Bringing it out beside fund papers confused you?
after: Did I confuse you by bringing it out beside the fund papers?

korean: 이쪽이 손에 덜 걸려요. 그걸로 하려고요.
before: This one catches my hand less. I'll take it.
after: This one is less awkward to hold. I'll take it.

before: Fortunately, within what I budgeted.
after: Fortunately, it's within my budget.

before: Leaving, but visiting again.
after: It means leaving, but coming back to visit.

before: Just an uneventful nap.
after: It was just an ordinary nap.

before: Then I won't force myself to wait over cold food.
after: Then I won't make myself wait while my food gets cold.

korean: 늘 괜찮냐고 묻고 나면 말을 바꾸게 돼요.
before: Asking if it's all right always makes me change it.
after: I always change my answer when I start by asking if it's all right.

before: Even the wholesale price was barely manageable.
after: They said even covering what they had paid for the goods was difficult.

korean: 오늘 못한 일을 잘한 일로 덮지는 않을래요.
before: I won’t try to make up for what I failed to do today by listing what I did well.
after: I won't cover up what I failed to do today by listing what I did well.

before: Shaking hands? Sit briefly.
after: Are your hands shaking? Sit for a moment.

before: Check the fallen person's side.
after: Check on the person who fell.

before: I'm hurt too. I'll stop my hands briefly.
after: I'm hurt too. I'll stop what I'm doing for a moment.

before: Watching only over there, I missed them.
after: I was so focused on them that I missed my own wounds.

before: A seal? Stop your hands first.
after: A seal? Keep your hands back first.

before: Don't overreach before the container.
after: Don't push yourself trying to open the container.

before: You'll help only if I tell their circumstances?
after: You'll help only if I tell you about their circumstances?

korean: 모르는 곳은 같이 물으러 가면 좋겠어요.
before: I'd like us to ask together where we don't know.
after: I'd like us to ask together about what we don't know.

korean: 마시라고 내민 건데, 그냥 두고 가기는 어렵군요.
before: I offered it for you to drink. Leaving it untouched feels difficult.
after: I offered it for you to drink. I find it hard to leave while it is untouched.

korean: 서류는 접었어도 확인할 대목은 남겨 두었습니다.
before: Folded, but I left the points to check marked.
after: I folded the papers, but left the points we need to check marked.

before: You give me a reason to free my hands.
after: With your help, I can put my work down.

korean: 모서리가 구겨질까 봐 가방을 누르고 있었습니다.
before: I held the bag down to keep the corners from creasing.
after: I held the book in the bag to keep its corners from creasing.

korean: 제 잔을 채우는 일은 자꾸 남은 뒤로 미루게 됩니다. 오늘도 그렇게 됐군요.
before: Filling mine keeps coming after the leftovers. Again today.
after: I keep putting off filling my own cup until everyone else has had some. I did it again today.

korean: 함께 마셔도 인사가 되는지 몰랐습니다. 그런 순서는 없던데요.
before: I did not know drinking together counted as greeting. That sequence was not in it.
after: I did not know drinking together could be a greeting. That step was not in the book.

korean: 쏟지 않게 가방 옆은 피해 두십시오.
before: Please keep it away from the bag so it doesn’t spill.
after: Please keep it away from the bag so it does not spill.

korean: 다만 두 뜻 가운데 어느 쪽을 약속하는지는 알고 싶습니다.
before: But I want to know which meaning I am promising.
after: But I want to know what I am promising.

korean: 그럼 안쪽에 앉겠습니다. 여기는 바람이 덜 드는군요.
before: Then I will sit inside. Less draft here.
after: Then I will sit farther inside. There is less of a draft here.

korean: 그 쪽을 다시 펴는 날이 있다는 것까지 남에게 맡기기는 조금 부끄럽습니다.
before: Entrusting even my return to that page to someone else feels embarrassing.
after: I would feel embarrassed to rely on someone else even to remember my page.

korean: 종이는 넉넉합니다. 필요하시면 한 장 드리겠습니다.
before: I have plenty of paper. A sheet, if you need one.
after: I have plenty of paper. I can give you a sheet if you need one.

korean: 규정을 외우면 쉬운데, 그 앞에 선 사람의 질문은 남더군요.
before: Reciting rules is easy. The person's questions remain.
after: Reciting rules is easy. But it does not answer the person's questions.

korean: 아까 멈춘 말은 조금 더 생각해 보았습니다.
before: I thought further about the words I stopped earlier.
after: I gave more thought to the words I left unfinished earlier.

korean: 지난번에 교리서라고 말하려 했습니다. 제가 그렇게 보일 때도 기다려 주십시오.
before: Last time I nearly called it doctrine. Please wait even when I seem like that.
after: Last time I almost called it a doctrinal text. Please give me time even when I seem about to make an excuse.

korean: 초대할 때는 둘이 함께 먹는다고 되어 있었는데요. 어디서 봤는지는요…….
before: An invitation means both eat together, it said. Where I read that...
after: It said that when you invite someone, you eat together. As for where I read that...

korean: 같이 먹고 싶다는 말만 하면 될 텐데 또 순서를 돌아왔습니다.
before: I could simply say I want company, but circled through procedure again.
after: I could simply say I want company, but I turned it into a matter of procedure again.

korean: 어떻게 해야 할지 몰라서 여쭌 건데, 그 말은 제가 이미 아는 사람 같습니다.
before: I asked because I did not know. Those words make me sound as though I already do.
after: I asked because I did not know what to do. You are speaking as though I already knew.

before: You would not believe 'doctrine' this time.
after: I doubt you would believe me if I called it 'doctrine' this time.

korean: 어느 대목에서 멈추셨는지 조용히 나누고 싶었습니다. 그 순서는 제가 정해도 되겠습니까?
before: I wanted to quietly share where we paused. May I choose that order?
after: I wanted to share the passage where we paused quietly. May I choose to do that first?

korean: 책에서는 이쯤에 말을 건네던데, 그게 어느 때인지 잘 모르겠습니다.
before: In the book, they spoke around now. I am unsure when 'now' is.
after: In the book, they spoke at about this point. I am not sure when that would be here.

before: I nearly waited too long over the book alone.
after: I nearly spent too long waiting and worrying over the book alone.

before: Choosing comfort brought me here.
after: I chose the seat I found comfortable, and it brought me here.

korean: 뜻만 전해지면 되죠. 익숙한 서약문으로 해 주세요.
before: The meaning matters. Use your familiar oath.
after: The meaning matters. Use the oath you're familiar with.

before: I'll listen slowly, even without memorized words.
after: I'll listen at your pace, even if you haven't memorized the words.

korean: 그 사람을 두고 서약만 옳았다고 말하지는 않겠습니다.
before: I will not leave them and call only the oath right.
after: I will not leave a person behind and claim only the oath matters.

korean: 같이 찾겠다는 말이 있으니 빈 종이를 두고도 도망치지 않겠습니다.
before: With your promise to search together, I will not flee the blank sheet.
after: With your promise to look for an answer together, I will not turn away from the blank sheet.

korean: 잊었다고 해야 시작할 수 있으면 또 괜찮다고 해 버릴 것 같습니다.
before: If starting requires claiming to forget, I may say I am fine again.
after: If starting over means saying I have forgotten, I may pretend I am fine again.

korean: 괜찮다는 답을 외워 둔 것처럼 빨리 하곤 했습니다.
before: I answered 'fine' so quickly, as though memorized.
after: I answered 'I'm fine' so quickly, as though I had memorized it.

before: If I arrange my expression first, you will miss it again.
after: If I compose my expression first, you may miss how I feel again.

korean: 다음 장보다 지금 옆에서 읽는 소리가 먼저 들립니다.
before: I hear your reading beside me before thinking of the next page.
after: I hear you reading beside me before I think of turning the next page.

before: Even finished, I will not reveal the ending.
after: Even if I finish first, I will not reveal the ending.

korean: 같이 읽자고 하고는 읽는 재미까지 덜어 드린 것 같아 마음이 쓰입니다.
before: I invited you to read together and fear I reduced your enjoyment.
after: I invited you to read with me, but I fear I made it less enjoyable for you.

korean: 결말은 각자 읽을 때까지 아껴 두겠습니다.
before: I will save the ending until we each read it.
after: I will save the ending until we have both read it.

korean: 오래 서 있다 마시는 것보다 좋습니다.
before: Better than after standing a long time.
after: It is better than drinking after being on my feet for so long.

korean: 종이 한 장인데 버리기가 어려워서 가져왔습니다.
before: Only one sheet, but hard to discard. I brought it.
after: It is only one sheet, but I could not bring myself to discard it. I brought it along.

korean: 그 종이에는 이제 사과 순서를 적지 않습니다.
before: That paper no longer carries an apology's procedure.
after: I no longer write instructions for apologizing on that paper.

korean: 제 옆에서 어떤 대답이 나올지도 이제 생각합니다.
before: Now I consider what answer may come beside me too.
after: Now I also think about how the person beside me might answer.

before: Has all been well?
after: Has everything been all right?

korean: 내일도 별일 없이 계셨는지, 그 말이 궁금해서 돌아왔습니다.
before: I came back wondering whether tomorrow too you would be quietly well.
after: I came back wanting to know that all was well, and hoping it will be tomorrow, too.

korean: 별일이 없었다는 대답도 듣고 싶습니다. 이번에는 책에 없어서 못 묻겠다는 말은 안 하겠습니다.
before: I want to hear 'nothing happened' too. This time no book's omission will stop me asking.
after: I want to hear about uneventful days, too. This time, I will not let the absence of a question in a book stop me from asking.

before: I will hold the front. The rear, please.
after: I will hold the front. Please watch the rear.

before: Wounds may come before equipment.
after: Let us check wounds before equipment.

korean: 이번에는 제 상처도 함께 봐 주시겠습니까?
before: Would you check my wounds together this time too?
after: Would you help me check my wounds this time, too?

before: Not in the oath, but I am truly happy now.
after: These words are not in the oath, but I am truly happy now.

korean: 서두르다 상처를 건드리지 않게 함께 옮겨 주세요.
before: Help move them without jarring the wound in haste.
after: Help me move them gently. We must not jar the wound in our haste.

korean: 조금 다쳤습니다. 제 장비를 봐 주시겠습니까?
before: A little hurt. Would you check my equipment?
after: I am a little hurt. Would you check my equipment?

korean: 지금은 제가 괜찮은지보다 모두의 걸음이 먼저입니다.
before: For now, everyone's steps come before questions about me.
after: For now, making sure everyone can walk comes before asking whether I am fine.

korean: 제 판단도 다시 살피겠습니다. 우선 같이 돌아가요.
before: I will review my judgment too. First, home together.
after: I will review my judgment too. First, let us get home together.

korean: 제 몫을 뒤로 미루지 않겠다는 말도 지키겠습니다.
before: I will keep my promise not to defer my own share too.
after: I will also keep my promise not to put off taking my own share.

korean: 좋게 들으려다가 제가 놓친 말이 있는 듯합니다.
before: Trying to hear the best, I seem to have missed some words.
after: I wanted to hear the best in your words, and I seem to have missed part of what you said.

before: Don't shake it out as scraps.
after: Don't shake them out as though they were scraps.

before: Watching my hands, I miss your words.
after: When I focus on my hands, I miss what you're saying.

before: I hear soft voices too. Speak comfortably.
after: I can hear you even when you speak softly. Use whatever voice is comfortable.

before: Less time at the guild than the barracks.
after: I've spent less time at the guild than at the barracks.

before: I can hear you softly now too.
after: I can hear you even when you speak softly now, too.

before: I'll retie it briefly.
after: I'll stop to retie it.

before: Herbs still scent my hands.
after: My hands still smell of herbs.

before: Stronger on my sleeve than my palms.
after: The smell's stronger on my sleeve than on my palms.

korean: 손에 든 것만 치우고 바로 먹을게요.
before: I'll clear what's in my hands and eat.
after: I'll put down what I'm holding and eat.

before: This time, bowl first.
after: This time, I'll pick up my bowl first.

before: It kept rising. I won't sing it.
after: The ending kept going up in pitch. I'd rather not sing it.

korean: 틀린 노래를 계속 들으면 괴롭지 않아요?
before: Isn't repeated wrong singing painful?
after: Isn't it painful hearing someone sing it wrong over and over?

before: Your face spoke before the bowl.
after: I could read the taste on your face before you said anything about the food.

before: A sip if the taste lingers.
after: Have a sip if the taste lingers.

before: That wasn't a face saying it wasn't bitter.
after: Your expression didn't say it wasn't bitter.

before: Parents can wait.
after: I'll talk about my parents another time.

before: I wanted to tell you roads I know.
after: I wanted to tell you about the roads I know.

korean: 약이 모자란 날은 손이 자꾸 멈춰요.
before: On medicine-short days, my hands keep stopping.
after: On days when medicine runs short, I keep hesitating over my work.

korean: 늘 한 사람만 더 보고 먹으려 해요.
before: Always just one more patient before eating.
after: I always tell myself I'll see one more patient before eating.

before: I'd like rest now too.
after: I'd like to rest now, too.

korean: 잔이 비었는데도 주전자에 손이 안 갔네요.
before: Empty cup, yet I never reached for the pitcher.
after: My cup was empty, but I never reached for the pitcher.

before: Moved closer, it's within reach now.
after: Now it's closer, I can reach it.

before: Less yawning on rising this time.
after: I yawned less when I got up this time.

before: Scratched it tidying in haste.
after: I scratched it while tidying in a hurry.

before: I nearly ignored it, then looked myself first.
after: I nearly ignored it, but then I took a look myself.

korean: 지금은 남은 것보다 손부터 보고 올래요.
before: Right now, hands before unfinished work.
after: Right now, I'll tend to my hands before my unfinished work.

before: Learning too late where you hurt is a shame.
after: I'd rather not find out too late where you're hurting.

korean: 그렇게 숨기시면 더 늦게 알게 돼요.
before: Hiding it delays my knowing.
after: Hiding it only keeps me from knowing sooner.

before: This cup today.
after: I'll use this cup today.

before: Mine first today.
after: I'll serve myself first today.

korean: 항상 챙겨 주셨는데 오늘은 제가 늦었네요.
before: You always care for me. Today I'm late.
after: You always look after me. Today I was slow to do the same for you.

before: Sunlight reached here.
after: The sunlight has reached this chair.

korean: 접던 천은 옆에 두었으니 얘기해 주세요.
before: The cloth's aside. Tell me.
after: I've put the cloth aside. Tell me.

korean: 가방은 아침에 보고 오늘은 같이 내려갈게요.
before: Bags tomorrow. Today I'll come down with you.
after: I'll sort the bags tomorrow. Today I'll come down with you.

before: I'll look for places ankles could catch.
after: I'll look for places where you could catch your foot.

korean: 제가 볼 수 있는 쪽도 알려 주세요.
before: Show me where I can inspect too.
after: Show me from somewhere I can see it, too.

before: Unknown? Leave it and look.
after: Don't know what it is? Leave it where it is and look.

korean: 같이 한 번 더 숨 쉬면 좋겠어요.
before: I'd like one more shared breath.
after: I'd like us to take one more breath together.

before: Not all moving at once.
after: Let's not all move at once.

before: No strength to speak? Just move your head.
after: No strength to speak? Just nod or shake your head.

before: No bottles out right now.
after: I won't take out any bottles right now.

before: I'll fill my water too.
after: I'll fill my water cup, too.

before: I'll speak immediately if struggling too.
after: I'll speak up right away if I'm struggling, too.

before: Heard. I'll be punctual too.
after: Heard you. I'll be on time, too.

korean: 손 아래 종이는 아직 누구 값에도 안 들어갔어요.
before: The paper under my hand belongs to no bargain yet.
after: The paper under my hand isn't part of any bargain yet.

before: This face's price changes with each guess.
after: The price of reading this face changes with every correct guess.

before: Unconfirmed words still.
after: It's still unconfirmed.

korean: 확인 전인 말 옆에는 오늘도 접은 자국을 남겼어요.
before: Unconfirmed words get a folded corner again today.
after: I'll fold the corner on an unconfirmed story again today.

before: Asking about my craft first.
after: You're asking about my craft first.

korean: 아직 값을 안 정했는데 벌써 빚을 지셨네요.
before: No price set, and you've already acquired a debt.
after: I haven't even set a price, and you've already decided you owe me.

before: I meant I forgot the price today.
after: I meant I'd forgotten to ask a price today.

before: Not immediately balancing the books, right?
after: You won't rush to balance the books, then?

korean: 잘 맞혀야만 들을 수 있는 말이면 좀 어렵네요.
before: Words earned only through correct guesses are difficult.
after: It's hard if I only get to hear you after I've guessed right.

before: Opening my escape route first.
after: You're leaving me a way out before I even ask.

korean: 할 일을 안 잡아 두니 이렇게 앉아 있을 수 있네요.
before: No work booked, and here I can sit.
after: I haven't booked any work, so I can sit here.

before: Not a story for a quick smile and answer.
after: That's not a story I can answer with a quick smile.

korean: 그것만 좋아서 여기까지 온 줄로 들리나요?
before: Do I sound as though I came here loving only that?
after: Do I sound as though I came here with nothing but fond memories?

korean: 길값 얘기를 하다 오늘은 계산이 잠깐 늦었네요.
before: Talking road prices slowed my counting briefly today.
after: Talking about the price of roads made me pause in my calculations today.

korean: 두 군데가 서로 모르는 게 있죠.
before: Each doesn't know something the other knows.
after: Each contains something the other doesn't.

korean: 제가 아직 못 정한 값을 너무 빨리 치르시네요.
before: You're paying a price I haven't chosen yet rather quickly.
after: You're paying a price I haven't even chosen to pay yet.

korean: 머무는 마음을 말했더니 농담할 값이 남지 않았네요.
before: Speaking of staying left no price for a joke.
after: Once I admitted I wanted to stay, I had no bargaining left for a joke.

korean: 제가 손 놓은 데 바로 손을 얹으시네요.
before: Your hand lands right where I lifted mine.
after: Your hand is reaching for the work I just put down.

before: Today I wanted it empty.
after: Today I wanted to leave my hands empty.

before: I used to call that wasteful easily too.
after: I used to be quick to call that a waste, too.

before: Writing plenty is convenient, yes?
after: It's convenient to write down plenty of promises, isn't it?

before: I'll promise for my own tongue first.
after: I'll start by promising to watch what I say.

korean: 잊을까 봐 적는 게 늘 좋은 건 아니네요.
before: Writing against forgetfulness isn't always good.
after: Writing things down so we won't forget isn't always better.

before: Even when the job ends, dinner together.
after: Even when the job ends, I'd like us to have dinner together.

korean: 돌려놓을 때 누가 먼저 알지 생각하면 어렵고요.
before: Harder when you consider who'll notice repayment first.
after: It's harder to put it back when you think about who will notice first.

korean: 제가 감출 말과 같이 책임질 말을 나눠 봐요.
before: Let's distinguish what I'll conceal from what we'll answer for together.
after: Let's separate what I'd conceal from what we'd take responsibility for together.

before: Oh, coming for nothing makes opening difficult.
after: Oh, coming without business makes it hard to start talking.

before: Cups to choose when I return, then.
after: Then there'll be cups to choose from when I return.

korean: 문과 식탁을 함께 보는 건 오늘도 제 선택이에요.
before: Seeing door and table together remains my choice today.
after: Today I can see both the door and the table, and still choose for myself.

before: Someone I wouldn't mind being tied to.
after: Someone I wouldn't mind staying tied to...

korean: 나갈 수 있는 제가 여기 있고 싶다는 말도 들어 주세요.
before: Hear that, free to leave, I want to be here.
after: Hear me when I say that I'm free to leave, and I want to be here.

before: My eyes priced it first.
after: I was putting a price on it before I'd even finished looking.

before: Before who won, I'll check who stood together.
after: Before asking who won, I'll check who stood with us.

before: If choosing here, choose together.
after: If we're making a choice here, let's make it together.

korean: 같이 얻은 건 같이 놓고 셀게요.
before: Shared gains go down for a shared count.
after: I'll lay out what we gained together so we can count it together.

korean: 큰 소문보다 오늘 얼굴이 먼저 남겠어요.
before: Today's faces will outlast the big rumors.
after: I'll remember the faces here longer than the grand rumors.

before: I stopped my tongue selling 'I'm fine' first.
after: I stopped myself before I could try to sell you an 'I'm fine.'

before: No conditions on rest too, right?
after: Rest doesn't come with conditions either, right?

korean: 입도 잠깐 손해 안 보고 쉴 수 있네요.
before: Even my tongue can rest without a loss briefly.
after: I can take a short break from talking without a loss, too.

before: I'll come first and just look at the seats.
after: I'll arrive early and simply look for a seat.

before: Even defeated, home together.
after: Even in defeat, let's go home together.

before: Even wrong, I'd like to hear the answer.
after: Even if my guess is wrong, I'd like to hear your answer.

before: I'll ask first about words we learned together.
after: I'll ask before passing on what we learned together.

before: I dislike being sold without knowing too.
after: I don't want my words sold without my knowing, either.

before: You should hear me there too.
after: You should be able to hear me from there, too.

before: At the table's end.
after: It's at the end of the table.

before: More overlapping footsteps than usual too.
after: I can hear more footsteps overlapping than usual, too.

before: Stone roads hold sound a long time.
after: Sound lingers on stone roads.

before: Even the smells at corners.
after: I even use the smells at street corners.

korean: 여기는 빵 냄새가 나는군요. 기억해 둘게요.
before: Bread here. I'll remember.
after: I smell bread here. I'll remember that.

korean: 저 빵 냄새가 나는 쪽을 기억해 볼게요.
before: I'll remember the way smelling of bread.
after: I'll remember the street that smells of bread.

before: My slipping hand startled me.
after: My hand slipped. It startled me.

before: Support the bottom. Less slipping.
after: Support the bottom. It won't slip as much.

before: Better here than my forest knot.
after: It works better here than the knot I used in the forest.

before: I can't see beyond the curtain well either.
after: I can't see past the curtain very well, either.

before: Through walls, direction is confusing.
after: It's hard to tell the direction through walls.

before: The water tells me where it is now.
after: Now the sound of water tells me where it came from.

korean: 손이 굳어서 시위를 놓칠 때도 있어요.
before: Sometimes my hands lock and I lose the bowstring.
after: Sometimes my hands freeze and I let go of the bowstring.

before: Joining as escort, I considered only the road.
after: When I joined as an escort, I thought only about the journey.

before: Much outside is new to her too.
after: Much of life outside the forest is new to her, too.

korean: 숲에서는 나무를 볼 때 먼저 규약을 떠올렸어요.
before: In the forest, trees first brought the code to mind.
after: In the forest, seeing a tree made me think of the code first.

before: I want to travel considering why I kept it.
after: As I travel, I want to keep thinking about why I followed it.

korean: 이 흠은 누가 오래 기대앉아서 났을까요?
before: Did someone leaning here for years make this mark?
after: Did years of people leaning here leave this mark?

korean: 저 벽만 지나면 손을 놓아도 괜찮겠어요.
before: Past that wall, letting go should be fine.
after: Once we are past that wall, I should be able to let go.

before: Turned where the bread smells.
after: I turned where I could smell bread.

before: Half closed should ease it.
after: Closing it halfway should keep some of the wind out.

korean: 어느 쪽이었어요? 저도 헷갈린 곳일지 몰라요.
before: Which? Perhaps one that confused me too.
after: Which one? Perhaps it confused me, too.

before: Then let's sit together from now.
after: Then let's sit together for a while.

korean: 놓친 소리가 있으면 서로 알려 줘요.
before: Tell each other any missed sounds.
after: Let's tell each other about any sounds the other missed.

before: Narrow, but room for both.
after: It's narrow, but there's room for both of us.

before: Today I recognized the stairs.
after: Today I recognized your footsteps on the stairs.

before: Not loud. You drag them a little.
after: Not loud. You drag your feet a little.

before: Then I truly stared only at the plate.
after: Back then, I really did just stare at the plate.

before: At first, unbearably noisy.
after: At first, it was unbearably noisy.

before: Hard to choose between them.
after: It's hard to choose between them.

before: Cold wind. Closing would be good.
after: The wind's cold. It would be good to close it.

before: Tell me only what you can see?
after: Could you tell me only what you can see?

before: From beside it, a little different.
after: It looks a little different from the side.

before: Listening for other sounds.
after: I'm listening for other sounds.

before: A little longer listening before moving.
after: I'd like to listen a little longer before we move.

before: Back home, water somewhere quiet.
after: When we're back, let's have water somewhere quiet.

before: Only their voices made me turn.
after: I turned only when I heard their voices.

before: Now find our shared way out.
after: Now let's find our way out together.

korean: 같이 천천히 가면 될 것 같아요.
before: Slowly together should work.
after: We should be able to do it slowly, together.

before: Leaning here, I hear less stone noise too.
after: Leaning here, I hear less of the echo from the stone, too.

korean: 오늘은 신발이 덜 울리는 길로 가요.
before: Today, a road where shoes echo less.
after: Today I'd like a road where our footsteps echo less.

before: Hear my voice? Come that way.
after: Can you hear my voice? Come toward it.

before: When we rest, water together first.
after: When we stop to rest, let's have water together first.

before: Ornel draws her bow beside her.
after: Ornel brings her bow close to her side.

korean: 저는 다리 많은 것을 잘 못 봐요.
before: Many-legged things are difficult for me.
after: Creatures with many legs frighten me.

before: Even a detour, would that be all right?
after: Would that be all right, even if it means a detour?

korean: 편한 일과 보여 주는 일은 달라요.
before: Enjoying it and showing it are different.
after: Enjoying it is different from wanting to show it.

before: Right now I'll hide my hands too.
after: Right now I'd rather keep my hands out of sight, too.

before: Not how far.
after: But not how far.

korean: 제 발 놓을 곳도 제가 알아야 해요.
before: I need to know where my feet go.
after: I need to know where I am going.

korean: 덮어 둔 크기는 다 뜬 뒤에 볼 거예요.
before: We'll see the covered size when it's finished.
after: You'll see what I'm making when it's finished.

korean: 길 확인한 말은 제가 먼저 할게요.
before: I'll announce the route check myself first.
after: I'll say when I've checked the route.

before: I like the knitting time.
after: I like spending time knitting.

before: Something I want to repay by hand.
after: Some kindnesses I want to repay with my own work.

korean: 실은 조금씩 줄어도 떠 놓은 건 남아요.
before: Yarn dwindles, but the knitting remains.
after: The yarn runs out. What I knit remains.

korean: 다가오지 않는 동안도 기다릴 수 있어요.
before: I can wait while they don't approach too.
after: I can wait even if they don't come closer.

before: The recipient has a part too.
after: The one receiving it has a say, too.

korean: 길 보는 건 저도 같이 할래요.
before: I want to share the scouting.
after: I want a share in checking the route.

before: Enough that you know.
after: It's enough that you know.

before: That's why I asked measurements.
after: That's why I asked for your measurements.

korean: 오늘 잰 치수는 다른 사람 것과 바꾸지 않을게요.
before: Today's measurements won't become someone else's.
after: I won't use your measurements for someone else.

before: Still something to repay.
after: I still have something to repay.

before: Not finishing quickly.
after: I'm not saying I'll finish quickly.

korean: 실 풀리는 소리 나도 듣고 있어요.
before: Even with unraveling sounds, I'm listening.
after: I hear you, even while I'm unraveling this.

korean: 손으로 남긴 건 말할 수 있어요.
before: I can tell what my hands left.
after: I can tell you what I made.

before: I won't sell the face I tried to capture too.
after: I won't sell the person I tried to capture in it, either.

before: Comfortable or not, someone waits.
after: Comfortable or not, there's someone waiting.

before: Giving it for you to wear.
after: I'm giving it to you to wear.

before: They keep hiding in my pocket.
after: I keep hiding them in my pockets.

korean: 모르는 건 모른 채 곁에 계시는 거군요.
before: You stay beside the unknowns, then.
after: You stay beside her even when you don't know, then.

before: Rush to understand and she hides.
after: Rush to understand her and she hides.

before: Don't send me off for few words.
after: Don't send me away just because I have little to say.

korean: 갚을 것 없는 날에도 이쪽은 비어 있어요.
before: This seat's free on debtless days too.
after: This seat is free even when you owe nothing.

korean: 기억하는 것과 바로 갚는 건 다를 수 있어요.
before: Remembering and immediate repayment can differ.
after: Remembering a kindness doesn't mean repaying it at once.

before: Comfort doesn't require abandoning memory.
after: Being at ease doesn't mean giving up the memory.

korean: 오늘은 받은 셈을 안 해도 되겠네요.
before: No need to count today's receipt, then.
after: No need to count what you received today, then.

korean: 두 잔 놓는 일은 오늘 셈에 안 넣어요.
before: Setting two cups doesn't enter today's accounts.
after: Setting out two cups doesn't go in the accounts.

korean: 걱정 말라고 말을 없애고 싶진 않아요.
before: I don't want reassurance to erase words.
after: I don't want your reassurance to mean I stop telling you.

before: Word before sunset.
after: I'll send word before sunset.

before: Today, ears before hands.
after: Today I'll listen instead of working.

korean: 뜨개질을 멈춘 손으로도 곁에 있을 수 있어요.
before: Even hands that stop knitting can stay beside you.
after: I can stop knitting and still stay beside you.

before: Clear floor.
after: There's room on the floor.

korean: 빈손인 건 봤어요. 얼굴 보고 반가웠고요.
before: I saw your empty hands. Your face made me glad.
after: I saw you came empty-handed. I was glad to see you.

korean: 오늘 받은 물은 따뜻했다는 것만 기억할래요.
before: I'll remember only today's water was warm.
after: I'll just remember that the water was warm today.

korean: 고쳐서 다시 쓰면 더 잘 알아봐요.
before: Mended and reused, I'll recognize it better.
after: Once it's mended and worn again, I'll recognize it even better.

before: Going together, I'll keep my hands free.
after: I'll keep my hands free so we can go together.

before: Saw together. Remember together.
after: We saw it together. We can remember together.

before: I won't choose it like repayment.
after: I won't make the choice as if I were repaying a debt.

before: My plan, briefly.
after: Let me tell you my plan briefly.

before: We can share helping hands.
after: We can share the work of helping.

korean: 받은 신세를 두고 먼저 가진 않을게요.
before: I won't leave first, abandoning a kindness received.
after: I won't leave first and disregard the help I received.

korean: 그래도 받아 둘게요. 손 빌려 줘서 고마워요.
before: I’ll accept it, then. Thank you for helping me.
after: I'll accept it, then. Thank you for helping me.

before: Remaining hands before losses.
after: Those who can still help come before counting losses.

before: I'll choose how my hands serve too.
after: I'll choose what work I take on, too.

before: I'll tell when I began.
after: I'll tell you when I began.

before: Want to see your face accepting too.
after: I want to see your face when you receive it, too.

korean: 다 갚았다는 말은 아직 안 했어요.
before: Haven't said everything's repaid yet.
after: I haven't said I've repaid everything yet.

before: Whether I am willing required asking me.
after: You still needed to ask whether I was willing.

before: Our first journey together.
after: This is our first journey together.

before: Easier to settle now.
after: It is easier to settle the money now.

before: Rich soup today.
after: The soup smells rich today.

korean: 그릇이 뜨거워서 옮길 때도 천을 댔죠.
before: Bowls so hot we carried them with cloth.
after: The bowls were so hot we carried them with cloths.

korean: 쉬는 날까지 벌 궁리를 하진 않았죠.
before: I did not plan earnings on days off too.
after: I did not plan to spend my days off thinking of earnings, too.

before: The owner hurried me before it cooled.
after: The owner urged me to eat before it cooled.

korean: 그 집 국은 입천장을 데기 쉬웠습니다.
before: That place's soup could scald your palate.
after: The soup there could burn the roof of your mouth.

before: Loose strap. I threaded it again.
after: The strap was loose. I threaded it through again.

before: Everyone should check their own other bags.
after: Everyone should check the rest of their own bags.

before: In Marento, always the same place.
after: In Marento, I always went to the same place.

before: No chance to act a new customer.
after: I had no chance to pretend I was a new customer.

before: Every day at the arena.
after: It was like that every day at the arena.

before: Both shoes before entering.
after: Let me shake out both shoes before entering.

before: Enduring comes last.
after: Enduring thirst should be the last resort.

before: Upright, the bottle keeps rolling off.
after: It keeps tipping over when I stand it up.

korean: 예. 아는 골목이 늘고, 돌아가는 배는 또 미뤘죠.
before: Yes. More familiar alleys, another postponed ship.
after: Yes. I knew more alleys, and kept putting off taking the ship.

before: From outside, all gladiators alike.
after: From the outside, all gladiators look alike.

before: Quite different at rest afterward, though.
after: But we were quite different when resting afterward.

korean: 씻고 밥 먹었습니다. 그게 제일 급했죠.
before: Washed and ate. Most urgent.
after: I washed and ate. Those were most urgent.

before: Ask where I am from: Kern.
after: Ask where I am from, and I say Kern.

before: Ask where I live: a pause.
after: Ask where I live, and I pause.

korean: 어디 사느냐는 물음에도 바로 답하고 싶고요.
before: And answer where I live without pausing.
after: And I want to answer where I live without pausing.

before: Now I know the road on returning.
after: Now I know my way back.

korean: 끈은 다 폈고, 이제 손도 좀 쉬어야겠네요.
before: Strap straight. Hands need rest now too.
after: The strap is straight. Now my hands need rest, too.

before: My duties, through to the end.
after: I will see my duties through to the end.

before: Kept moving to the next story.
after: We kept moving on to the next story.

before: Missing tomorrow's waking would be troublesome.
after: It would be troublesome to oversleep tomorrow.

korean: 방금 하던 건 내일 마저 들어요.
before: The unfinished story tomorrow.
after: Let us finish the story tomorrow.

before: If tired that day, I will say.
after: If I am tired that day, I will say so.

korean: 그럼 급한 용건은 둘 다 없군요.
before: Then neither has urgent business.
after: Then neither of us has urgent business.

before: Bag aside, room to stretch our legs.
after: With the bag aside, we have room to stretch our legs.

before: One can forget a garment.
after: Anyone can forget a garment.

before: Quite a few Torva roads walked.
after: They have carried me along quite a few roads in Torva.

korean: 신발을 버릴 만큼 나쁜 날만 있진 않았죠.
before: Not every day was bad enough to discard these.
after: I do not want to discard all the days I spent in these shoes.

before: Just do not burn your tongue. Hurrying again.
after: Just do not burn your tongue. You are hurrying again.

korean: 이번에는 짐을 두고 밥 먹으러 가겠습니다.
before: This time, I’ll leave my bag here and go eat.
after: This time, I will leave my bag here and go eat.

before: My assigned things are ready.
after: Everything I am responsible for is ready.

before: Do not touch on appearance alone.
after: Do not touch it just because it looks safe.

before: Curious indeed. Closer look.
after: It is curious. Let me take a closer look.

before: Shaking hands? Set it down briefly.
after: Are your hands shaking? Set it down briefly.

before: Back home, a generous meal.
after: When we return, I want a generous meal.

before: Stop here once.
after: Stop here for a moment.

before: Things to check before entering.
after: There are things to check before entering.

before: Breath before packs.
after: Catch your breath before lifting the packs.

before: I will check my movement.
after: I will check how well I can move.

before: Look at my side today too.
after: Please check on me today, too.

before: Hands still while resting.
after: Keep your hands still while resting.

before: Glad to see this road on returning.
after: I am glad to see this road again on our return.

before: Terms together first this time.
after: Let us review the terms together first this time.

korean: 마렌토에 남은 얘기를 조금 해 볼까요?
before: Shall I share a little of staying in Marento?
after: Shall I tell you a little about my time in Marento?

before: Thought you would come down. Poured it.
after: I thought you would come down, so I poured water.

before: Downstairs as soon as work ends.
after: I will come downstairs as soon as work ends.

before: Even if you need some, ask before taking it.
after: Even if you need some, ask before taking any.

korean: 쓰임을 알면 내줄지 정할 수 있어요.
before: Knowing the use lets me decide.
after: Knowing what you'll use it for lets me decide.

before: Just room for the packet.
after: Just leave room for the packet.

korean: 오늘 거래 얘기는 식사 뒤에 해요.
before: Today's business after dinner.
after: Today's business can wait until after dinner.

before: Two kinds of cloth.
after: There are two kinds of cloth.

before: Wipe here to keep them separate.
after: Wipe here. Keep that cloth separate.

korean: 그런 식으로는 제가 값을 깎은 이유를 설명해야 하죠.
before: That demands explaining why I discounted.
after: That would mean explaining why I gave them a discount.

before: Well-dried ones first.
after: Choose the well-dried ones first.

korean: 겉만 보고 한꺼번에 넣으면 다시 해야 해요.
before: Dumping them together on looks alone means starting over.
after: Mix them just because they look alike and you'll have to start over.

korean: 섞이면 다시 나누는 시간이 더 들어요.
before: Mixed, they take longer to separate.
after: Once mixed, they take longer to separate.

korean: 값을 맞춰 주면 긴 설명이 필요 없거든요.
before: Agree the price, and long explanations vanish.
after: Agree on the price, and we can skip the long explanations.

before: No rolling. Easier to see.
after: They won't roll, and they'll be easier to count.

before: Once close, no medicine charges.
after: Once we're friends, no charges for medicine.

before: Deliberately blank, not forgotten.
after: I left it blank deliberately. I didn't forget.

before: Don't extend my chosen exception.
after: Don't extend an exception I chose to make.

korean: 오늘은 이렇게 받겠어요. 다음 값은 따로 정해요.
before: This price today. Next time, separately agreed.
after: This is today's price. We'll agree on the next one separately.

before: Checking for mixed contents.
after: I'm checking that nothing else got mixed in.

before: Window after the checks.
after: I'll open the window after checking.

korean: 향만 맡으려고 열어 두면 못 쓰게 돼요.
before: Leaving it open for scent spoils it.
after: Leaving it open for the scent will spoil the ingredients.

korean: 오늘 일 얘기면 제가 먼저 할게요.
before: If today's work, I'll begin.
after: If it's about today's work, I'll begin.

before: Dinner here without introductions.
after: We can eat dinner here without introductions.

before: I’ll address you exactly as it’s written.
after: I'll address you exactly as it's written.

before: Later, sold directly outside.
after: Later, I sold directly outside the forest.

korean: 말한 데서 기다려 주시니 덜 불편하네요.
before: Waiting where I stop makes it easier.
after: It's easier if you wait when I stop speaking.

korean: 약초 다루는 손은 쉽게 안 바뀌어요.
before: Hands handling herbs don't change easily.
after: It's hard to change the way you handle herbs.

before: Quiet only at forest talk, you say?
after: You say I only go quiet when the forest comes up?

before: Left as it is, the sound comes through.
after: I can hear it with the window as it is.

korean: 덜 받은 칸도 남한테 읽히려고 쓴 건 아니에요.
before: Reduced entries weren't written for others to read either.
after: I didn't write down those discounts for others to read, either.

korean: 그리운 걸 바로 고칠 물건은 없어요.
before: No object immediately fixes longing.
after: An object won't make longing disappear at once.

before: Medicine came out first.
after: I started talking about medicine instead.

korean: 안 사도 된다는 말을 또 하게 되네요.
before: Saying 'no purchase needed' again.
after: Let me say it again: you don't have to buy anything.

korean: 틀린 글씨 값을 그렇게 매기진 마세요.
before: Don't price a writing mistake like that.
after: Don't turn an error in my writing into a demand for free goods.

before: Start with ingredient condition.
after: Start by checking the condition of the ingredients.

korean: 그런 기대를 받으면 값을 못 정해요.
before: I can't price that expectation.
after: I can't put a price on that expectation.

korean: 기대를 맞추려고 모르는 걸 안다고 하긴 싫어요.
before: I won't pretend knowledge to meet it.
after: I won't pretend to know things just to meet it.

before: Only with Aenwyn is my name complete.
after: My name is only complete with Aenwyn.

korean: 얘기할 때마다 사람을 비켜 줘야 하네요.
before: Every sentence, you must move aside.
after: You have to move aside with every sentence.

korean: 오가는 사람이 적어야 말이 잘 들려요.
before: Fewer passersby, clearer words.
after: With fewer people passing, we can hear each other better.

korean: 오늘도 값은 셌지만 그 얘기만 하진 않았어요.
before: Counted prices today, but discussed more than that.
after: I counted prices today, but we talked about more than that.

before: Truly nothing brought.
after: I really brought nothing.

before: Even the drafty door.
after: Yes. Even the drafty one.

before: No ledger. Light hands.
after: No ledger. Less to carry.

korean: 다만 매번 그 얘기부터 꺼내고 싶진 않죠.
before: But not as every opening subject.
after: But I don't want to begin every conversation with it.

before: Today, what happened here.
after: Today, I'll talk about what happened here.

korean: 싫어도 기다리셨다는 말을 나중에 듣긴 싫어요.
before: I don't want later news you waited unwillingly.
after: I don't want to hear later that you waited unwillingly.

korean: 찾은 게 쓸 만한지는 따로 봐요.
before: Finding and usefulness need separate checks.
after: Finding it is one thing. Knowing whether it is useful is another.

before: Ahead before accounts now.
after: Watch ahead for now. Accounts later.

before: 'Everything to you' can wait.
after: 'Leave everything to you' can wait.

before: Anything hidden while enduring?
after: Have you hidden any pain while holding on?

before: No time to spare necessities.
after: This is no time to skimp on necessities.

before: Enough to stiffen my hands completely.
after: That left my hands completely stiff.

before: After great battles, check wounds especially.
after: Check wounds especially carefully after major battles.

before: No immediate marching because there's time.
after: No need to march on immediately just because there's time.

before: Pretending delays the checks!
after: Pretending to be fine delays the checks!

before: No asking medicine prices first now!
after: No asking about medicine prices before getting help!

before: My hand's movement first.
after: I'll check how well I can move my hand first.

before: No claims I'll soon be fine.
after: I won't claim I'll be fine soon.

before: First, the faces who returned alive.
after: First, check on those who returned alive.

korean: 봉투 입구를 접어 자기 쪽에 둔다.
before: She folds the packet's mouth toward herself.
after: She folds the opening of the packet toward herself.

korean: 정리하지 않은 말도 들을 수 있어요.
before: I can hear unorganized words too.
after: I can listen even if you haven't organized your thoughts.

korean: 제가 적을 것만 말하시려는 것 같아서 조금 멀게 들리네요.
before: Speaking only for my notes sounds a little distant.
after: Speaking only to help me take notes feels a little distant.

korean: 제가 언제 펼지 기다려 주시면, 그때 질문도 같이 할게요.
before: Wait until I open mine, and I'll ask questions then too.
after: I'll ask questions when I've opened mine, too.

before: I'll note the time outside the notebook too.
after: I'll keep the time somewhere besides my notebook, too.

korean: 사람 수보다 제가 본 쪽을 묻는군요.
before: Asking what I saw, rather than how many saw it.
after: You're asking what I saw, rather than how many people saw it.

before: Until another check, blank.
after: I'll leave it blank until I've checked again.

korean: 손을 멈추면 말을 또 삼킬까 봐 식탁을 문지르고 있었어요.
before: I feared still hands would make me swallow my words again.
after: I feared that keeping my hands still would make me swallow my words again.

before: Would you still mean the same now?
after: Would you still mean the same thing now?

before: No other conclusions meanwhile.
after: I won't reach any other conclusions while you think.
