korean: 생각하시는 동안은 질문을 더 늘리지 않을게요.
before: No multiplying questions while you think.
after: And I won't add more questions while you think.

korean: 잘 지내고 싶어서 뜻을 묻는 거예요.
before: I ask the meaning because I want us to get along.
after: I ask what you mean because I want us to get along.

korean: 제가 적어 둔 뜻이 틀렸을 수도 있겠네요.
before: Perhaps my recorded meaning was wrong.
after: Perhaps I wrote down the wrong meaning.

korean: 펜은 나중에 들게요. 지금은 그 소리를 듣고 싶어요.
before: Pen later. Now I want your voice.
after: The pen can wait. Right now, I want to hear you.

korean: 아까 물은 말의 뜻은 아직 듣고 싶어요.
before: I still want the meaning I asked for earlier.
after: I still want to understand what I asked about earlier.

korean: 나중에 읽을 질문만 남기려던 건 아닌데요.
before: I didn't only want questions saved for later.
after: I didn't just want to save my questions for later.

korean: 질문이 싫으신지 제가 미리 답해 버렸네요.
before: I answered for you whether you'd dislike it.
after: I answered for you by assuming you wouldn't like it.

korean: 노트 끈을 묶기 전에 여쭤볼 게 있어요.
before: Something to ask before tying the notebook.
after: There was something I wanted to ask before tying the notebook shut.

korean: 아침에는 어느 자리에서 드시는지도 물어봐도 될까요?
before: May I ask your breakfast seat too?
after: May I also ask where you sit for breakfast?

korean: 겹친 잔 자국은 오늘도 조금 더 늘었네요.
before: More overlapping cup rings today too.
after: There are more overlapping cup rings today, too.

korean: 익숙한 말도 누군가 처음 가르쳐 줬겠지요?
before: Someone taught those familiar words once too, surely?
after: Someone must have taught you those familiar words once, too?

korean: 제가 방금 들은 말로 같이 웃고 싶어서 묻는 거예요.
before: I ask because I want to share the laugh in those words.
after: I ask because I want to share in the laughter those words bring.

korean: 그럼 지금 맛있다고 해도 조금 늦은 대박인가요?
before: Then am I too late to say it’s delicious?
after: Then am I too late to say it's delicious?

korean: 음식에 놀랐다는 말은 아직 입에 잘 붙지 않아요.
before: Surprise at food still doesn't come naturally to my tongue.
after: It still feels strange to speak of being surprised by food.

korean: 하루를 어떻게 나눠 쓰는지 노트에 그려 보다가 멈췄어요.
before: I stopped midway through sketching a day's divisions.
after: I stopped halfway through sketching how a day is divided.

korean: 하루가 짧다고들 하시는데, 쉬는 때는 어떻게 고르나요?
before: You call days short. How do you choose rest?
after: You say days are short. How do you decide when to rest?

korean: 함께 가만히 있는 시간도 어떻게 고르는지 알고 싶었어요.
before: I wanted to know how you choose shared stillness too.
after: I wanted to know how you choose to spend quiet time together, too.

korean: 배고픈 때와 일이 끝나는 때가 다른 날도 적어 볼게요.
before: I'll note days hunger and finishing work don't coincide too.
after: I'll also note the days when hunger and the end of work come at different times.

korean: 하루를 다 쓰지 않고 쉬는 방법이 자꾸 생각나요.
before: I keep considering resting without exhausting a day.
after: I keep thinking about resting before the whole day is spent.

korean: 학술 조사라고 적었는데 읽는 동안 조사를 잊었어요.
before: Marked 'academic research.' Reading, I forgot the research.
after: It is marked 'academic research.' But as I read, I forgot about the research.

korean: 다른 데서 웃었으면 그 이유도 들을 수 있겠어요.
before: Different laughs could lead to different reasons.
after: If we laugh at different parts, we could discuss why.

korean: 조사라는 말은 핑계가 조금 섞였어요. 그래도 읽는 재미는 남겨 두고 싶어요.
before: Research was partly an excuse. I still want the reading's pleasure.
after: Research was partly an excuse. I still want the pleasure of reading it.

korean: 같은 책에서 다른 곳을 짚는 이야기를 더 듣고 싶어요.
before: I'd like more stories of noticing different parts in one book.
after: I'd like to hear more about how we notice different things in the same book.

korean: 노트를 펴 놓으니 음식 냄새보다 이름부터 떠오르네요.
before: Open, it brings food names before their smells.
after: When I open it, I see food names before I notice the smells.

korean: 먹어 본 것과 궁금한 것을 같이 짚어 봐요.
before: Let's compare tasted dishes and curiosities together.
after: Let's compare the dishes we've tried with the ones we're curious about.

korean: 별표를 많이 붙이면 전부 중요한 게 되나요? 또 표시부터 늘릴 뻔했네요.
before: Would enough stars make everything important? Nearly more marks again.
after: Would enough stars make everything important? I nearly added more marks again.

korean: 먹어 본 음식에는 오늘도 작은 표시를 해 뒀어요.
before: Today's tasted dishes have small marks too.
after: I made small marks by the dishes I tried today, too.

korean: 학술 조사라고 말을 꺼내면 또 어려워지겠지요?
before: Starting with 'academic research' would complicate it again?
after: Would starting with 'academic research' complicate things again?

korean: 교리서라고 하시면 저도 노트는 꺼내지 않을게요. 조금 기다릴 수 있어요.
before: If you mean it’s a book of doctrine, I won’t take out my notebook. I can wait a little.
after: If you mean it's a book of doctrine, I won't take out my notebook. I can wait a little.

korean: 식기 전에 먹어야 하는데 적을 게 많네요.
before: Food before cooling, but so much to record.
after: I should eat before it cools, but there is so much to record.

korean: 냄새부터 적으면 맛을 잊을까요? 아니면 반대일까요?
before: Smell first and forget taste? Or the reverse?
after: If I start with the smell, will I forget the taste? Or the other way around?

korean: 그냥 같이 먹자는 뜻이었군요. 네, 펜은 그릇에서 먼 쪽에 놓을게요.
before: Simply eating together. Yes, pen away from the bowl.
after: We are simply eating together. Yes, I will keep the pen away from the bowl.

korean: 원래 이 맛이 궁금해서 폈는데 노트 때문에 기다리게 됐어요.
before: I opened it for curiosity about taste. Now the notebook makes us wait.
after: I opened it because I was curious about the taste. Now the notebook is delaying our meal.

korean: 아까 조용해서 다들 놀라지 않았나 봐요. 저만 늦게 웃었네요.
before: Earlier was quiet, so perhaps no surprise. Only I laughed late.
after: It was quiet earlier, so perhaps it was not surprise. I was the only one who laughed late.

korean: 조용히 좋을 때도 대박이라고 해도 되나요? 크기는 상관없나요?
before: Quiet pleasure too? Does its size matter?
after: Even quiet pleasure? Does it have to be something big?

korean: 쉬운 말 옆에 늦게 알아들은 때도 적어 놓을게요.
before: Beside the simple word, I'll note my late understanding.
after: Beside that simple word, I will note that I understood it late.

korean: 그럼 아주 작게 말하는 대박도 있겠군요?
before: Then an awesome spoken very softly exists too?
after: Then you can say 'awesome' very softly, too?

korean: 지금 좋았다고 먼저 말하고 나서 써 볼게요. 또 늦어도 알아들어 주실래요?
before: I'll start by saying I liked it. Even late again, will you understand?
after: I will start by saying I liked it. Even if I am late again, will you understand?

korean: 오늘 장에는 펼치다 말았다는 것도 적을게요. 그건 같이 본 일이니까요.
before: I'll note today's abandoned opening too. We saw that together.
after: I will note that I did not open the first page today, too. We saw that together.

before: Writing 'same' leaves too many faces out.
after: Writing 'the same' would leave too many people out.

korean: 나에린에 보낼 말과 여기 남길 말을 고를 때 옆에 계셔도 되겠어요?
before: May you stay while I choose words for Naerin and here?
after: Would you stay while I choose what to say to Naerin, and what to say here?

korean: 듣던 이야기로는 고를 수 없는 일이 많아요.
before: Many choices can't be made from the stories I heard.
after: Many choices cannot be made from what I have heard alone.

korean: 노트를 펴도 이름을 적을 칸 앞에서 자꾸 멈추네요.
before: Even open, I stop before the name entry.
after: Even with the notebook open, I pause before the space for a name.

korean: 이름을 못 들었다고 그냥 지나가게 되네요.
before: Without a name heard, I simply pass them by.
after: If I have not heard their name, I tend to pass them by.

korean: 말하면서 놓친 것이 떠오를 수도 있겠네요.
before: Speaking might recall something missed.
after: Talking might bring back something we missed.

korean: 이름을 들을 틈이 없던 분부터 자꾸 떠올라서 노트를 편 거예요.
before: Those I couldn't ask names of keep returning. That's why I opened it.
after: I keep thinking of the people whose names I could not ask. That is why I opened it.

korean: 이름을 지어 채우지 않을게요. 빈칸도 오래 남겨 둘 수 있겠어요.
before: No invented names. I can keep blanks long too.
after: I will not invent names. I can leave spaces blank for a long time, too.

korean: 모르는 이름을 비워 둔 칸은 지우지 않았어요.
before: I didn't erase the space for an unknown name.
after: I kept the space for the name I do not know.

korean: 덮는 소리가 너무 컸나요? 제 질문이 갑자기 싫어졌어요.
before: Too loud? Suddenly I disliked my question.
after: Was that too loud? Suddenly I did not like my own question.

korean: 정리를 잘하면 아무렇지 않은 말만 남을 거예요.
before: Well-organized thoughts might leave only harmless words.
after: If I organize my thoughts too neatly, I may leave out everything difficult to say.

korean: 얘기까지 그만할 뻔했어요. 아직 듣고 계시다면 다시 말할게요.
before: Nearly stopped talking too. If you're listening, I'll try again.
after: I nearly stopped talking, too. If you are listening, I will try again.

korean: 오늘은 누구와 함께 돌아왔는지를 제 손으로 적고 싶어요. 그게 제 기록이니까요.
before: Today I want to write whom I returned with myself. My record.
after: Today I want to write down whom I returned with, in my own words.

korean: 다음 장을 붙이더라도 이 칸은 이대로 두고 싶어요.
before: Even adding pages, I want this space preserved.
after: Even if I add pages, I want to keep this space.

korean: 두 종이를 겹치면 쉬운데 오늘은 나란히 놓았어요.
before: Overlapping would be easy. Today, side by side.
after: It would be easy to overlap them. Today, I will leave them side by side.

korean: 아직 읽어 드릴 말은 아니어도 빈칸으로 두진 않을게요.
before: Not ready to read aloud, but not left blank.
after: I am not ready to read it aloud, but I have not left it blank.

korean: 두 쪽을 같이 읽어도 제 말이 될 수 있다는 걸 이제 알겠어요.
before: Now I see both pages together can still be my voice.
after: Now I see that both pages can be in my voice.

korean: 종이를 나눠 놓아도 두 쪽 다 제가 쓴 말이네요.
before: Separated sheets, both still my words.
after: Separate sheets, but both still hold my words.

korean: 펜을 놓고 나니 무슨 얘기였는지 더 잘 들리네요.
before: Putting the pen down makes your story clearer.
after: When I put the pen down, I hear your story more clearly.

korean: 적지 않고 지나가면 잊을까 봐 늘 서둘렀어요.
before: I always rushed, fearing unwritten stories lost.
after: I always hurried to write, afraid I would lose stories I left unwritten.

korean: 오늘은 잊어버릴 수 있어도 같이 듣는 쪽을 고르고 싶어요.
before: Today, even risking forgetting, I want to listen together.
after: Today, even if I might forget something, I want to listen with you.

before: I asked too much of my own curiosity, didn't I?
after: I asked too many questions just to satisfy my curiosity, did I not?

korean: 질문을 받을 생각은 하면서도 준비가 늦었네요.
before: I expected questions, yet prepared slowly.
after: I expected questions, yet I still took a while to feel ready.

korean: 모두 약속하면 지킬 수 있을지부터 묻게 되네요.
before: Promising all makes me question whether I could keep it.
after: If I promise all of it, I wonder whether I could keep my word.

before: A promise to record missed days too.
after: Then I will also promise to record the days we could not meet.

korean: 처음부터 맞혔다고 적고 싶은 건 아닌데 가리려 한 마음은 비슷했네요.
before: I don't want to claim I always knew, but covering felt similar.
after: I do not want to claim I always knew. Covering it up felt much the same.

korean: 틀렸던 제가 다음 장에서 달라지는 거겠네요.
before: My mistaken self changes on the next page.
after: On the next page, I can show how I changed after that mistake.

korean: 이번에 확인한 순서도 빠뜨리지 않고 말씀드릴게요.
before: The verification sequence too, without omissions.
after: I will include how we checked, too, without leaving out any steps.

korean: 맞게 말했는지보다, 누구와 웃었는지가 먼저 떠올라요.
before: Before whether I said it right, I remember whom I laughed with.
after: Before remembering whether I said it right, I remember whom I laughed with.

korean: 지우면 다음에 또 처음 묻는 말이 되겠어요.
before: Then next time I'd ask as though new again.
after: Then I would ask about it next time as though I had never heard it before.

korean: 헷갈리는 말 옆에는 지우지 않은 흔적이 남았어요.
before: The confusing phrase still has its unerased traces.
after: The traces of my confusion are still there. I have not erased them.

korean: 보고서에 넣을 칸이 모자란데도 여기에 앉았어요.
before: Report space is short. Still, I sat here.
after: There is little room in my report. Still, I chose to sit here.

korean: 남길 수 있는 말만 고르지 않아도 되겠어요.
before: No need to select only preservable words.
after: There is no need to choose only words worth recording.

korean: 지금 같이 듣는 소리는 적지 않아도 제게 남을 것 같아요. 조금만 더 계세요.
before: I think today's shared sounds will remain unwritten too. Stay a little.
after: I think I will remember what I heard with you today even without writing it down. Stay a little.

korean: 향을 맡아도 오늘은 노트를 찾지 않을게요.
before: Even smelling them, no notebook today.
after: Even while enjoying the scents, I will keep my notebook closed today.

korean: 노트가 없어도 여기서는 손이 덜 허전하네요.
before: Without it, my hands feel less empty here.
after: Here, my hands feel less empty even without it.

korean: 잔을 놓는 손을 보고 나서야 누가 앉았는지 알았어요.
before: Only seeing your hand place it told me who sat here.
after: I only knew who had sat here when I saw your hand set down the cup.

korean: 여기서 함께 본 얼굴이 늘어나서 다시 앉고 싶었던 거예요.
before: More shared faces made me want this seat again.
after: As I came to know more of the faces here, I wanted to return to this seat.

korean: 누가 함께 있었는지 쓰니까 보고서와는 다른 말이 나왔어요.
before: Writing our company brought words unlike the report's.
after: Writing about those with me brought out words different from my report.

korean: 이제는 어디까지 봤는지보다 누구와 봤는지도 말하고 싶어요.
before: Now I want to tell not only how far, but with whom.
after: Now I want to say not only how far I went, but whom I went with.

korean: 길어져도 중간에 제 말로 바꾸지 않을게요.
before: However long, I won't replace them with my words midway.
after: However long it takes, I won't interrupt to replace your words with mine.

korean: 제 문장이 틀려도 제 손으로 고치고 싶어요. 그동안 듣고 계시면 좋겠어요.
before: Even wrong sentences, I want my own hand correcting. Please listen meanwhile.
after: Even when my sentences are wrong, I want to correct them myself. Please listen while I do.

korean: 길어진 말은 줄이기 전에 한 번 읽어 드리고 싶어요.
before: Before shortening these growing words, I'd like to read them once.
after: Before shortening this growing account, I would like to read it through once.

korean: 손이 먼저 가방으로 갔네요. 펜이 없는 줄 알고 잠깐 놀랐어요.
before: Hand to bag first. Missing the pen startled me briefly.
after: My hand went to my bag first. Not finding the pen startled me for a moment.

korean: 또 전부 남겨야 할 이야기가 되는군요.
before: Again, a story requiring every detail preserved.
after: That would make it another story where every detail had to be preserved.

korean: 오늘은 놓친 분이 없는지 저도 세어 볼게요.
before: Today I'll count for missing people too.
after: Today I will also check that no one is missing.

korean: 안 보이는 곳은 서로 말해 주기로 해요.
before: Tell each other our blind spots.
after: Let us tell each other what we cannot see.

korean: 제가 본 모양도 말씀드릴게요. 같은지 들어 봐요.
before: I'll describe its shape too. Listen for agreement.
after: I will describe its shape, too. Tell me whether it matches what you saw.

korean: 오늘의 발견에는 함께 본 분도 적고 싶어요.
before: Today's discovery should include who saw it together.
after: The record of today's discovery should include everyone who saw it together.

korean: 지금 본 것을 믿을게요. 함께 움직여요.
before: I'll trust what I saw now. Move together.
after: I will trust what I saw. Let us move together.

korean: 적을 말이 많지만 지금은 손을 빌려드릴게요.
before: Much to record. Now, helping hands.
after: There is much to record. Now it is time to help.

korean: 무사히 끝나서 좋아요. 이번에는 이 말부터 할래요.
before: Glad it ended safely. Those words first this time.
after: I am glad it ended safely. Those words come first this time.

before: Heard stories alone cannot decide this.
after: What we have heard alone cannot decide this.

korean: 모르는 점은 남겨 둔 채 준비부터 맞춰 봐요.
before: Unknowns can remain while we agree preparations.
after: We can agree on preparations even with some things still unknown.

before: Back home, ask each other the missed stories.
after: When we are back, let us ask each other about the things we missed.

korean: 괜찮다는 말만 믿고 지나가고 싶지는 않아요.
before: I don't want to pass on 'fine' alone.
after: I do not want to report only that someone said 'I am fine.'

korean: 참는 모습을 적고 싶지는 않아요. 쉬어 주세요.
before: I don't want endurance notes. Rest, please.
after: I do not want a record of how long you endured. Please rest.

korean: 괜찮을 거라고 적기 전에 도움부터 청할게요.
before: Before recording optimism, I'll ask for help.
after: Before writing that I will be fine, I will ask for help.

korean: 늦기 전에 말씀드릴게요. 저도 지금 쉬어야 해요.
before: Before too late: I need rest now too.
after: Before it is too late, I will say it: I need rest now, too.

korean: 물은 마셨나요? 저도 노트보다 잔부터 들게요.
before: Had water? Cup before notebook for me too.
after: Have you had water? I will take my cup before my notebook, too.

korean: 열지 않아도 알아볼 수 있는 것부터 보겠어요.
before: First, what we can learn without opening.
after: First, let us see what we can learn without opening it.

before: Back. Report and notebook need separate words.
after: We are back. I need different words for the report and the notebook.

korean: 기록보다 먼저 인사할래요. 함께 와서 좋았어요.
before: Greeting before records. Glad we came together.
after: A greeting before the records: I am glad we came back together.

korean: 졌어도 들을 이야기는 남아요. 함께 돌아가요.
before: Even defeated, stories remain. Home together.
after: Even in defeat, there are stories left to tell. Let us go home together.

korean: 사절로 골라졌을 때 이야기를 하고 싶어요.
before: I want to tell when I was chosen envoy.
after: I want to tell you about when I was chosen as envoy.

before: Hesitations the report won't include too.
after: And about the doubts I will not put in my report.

korean: 같은 것을 봐도 제 말로 남기려고 해요.
before: Even shared sights, my own words.
after: Even what we saw together should be in my own words.

korean: 종이에 남길 말부터 고르지 않아도 편해요.
before: It’s a relief not to choose what to write down before I speak.
after: It is a relief not to choose what to write down before I speak.

korean: 익숙한 말도 오늘 뜻은 다시 듣고 싶어요.
before: Even familiar words, I'd like today's meaning again.
after: Even with familiar words, I would like to hear what you mean today.

korean: 새 말을 적기 전에 그때 뜻부터 맞춰 보고 싶어요.
before: Before new words, agree the old meaning.
after: Before adding new words, let us agree on what the old ones meant.

before: I don't want to decide alone and announce.
after: I do not want to decide alone and simply announce my conclusion.

korean: 필요한 일은 확인하되 제 이야기는 접어 둘게요.
before: Necessary checks, but my story stays closed.
after: I will make the necessary checks, but I will not share my story now.

korean: 식탁에서 큰소리로 웃다가 둘만 남자 굳는다.
before: Her loud table laughter freezes when only two remain.
after: Her loud laughter at the table stops when only the two of you remain.

korean: 둘이 남으면 아까 하던 말도 잘 안 나와요.
before: Alone together, even those words won't come.
after: When it's just us, even those words won't come.

korean: 둘이서는 무슨 말을 해야 할지 모르겠네요.
before: Just us, I don't know what to say.
after: When it's just us, I don't know what to say.

before: Warm when I ate. Good.
after: It was warm when I ate it. Good, too.

before: Not practicing.
after: I'm not practicing.

before: Just stiff hands.
after: My hands are just stiff.

korean: 그냥 풀고 있는 손도 보여 드려야 하는 건가요?
before: Must I display even stretching hands?
after: Must even stretching my hands be a show?

before: Everyone saw? I finished first!
after: Did everyone see? I finished first!

before: Oh, drank too fast. Breathless.
after: Oh, I drank too fast. I need a breath.

korean: 그런 값 걸고 한 말은 아니었는데요.
before: I didn't stake that on it.
after: I never agreed to that stake.

korean: 이번 잔엔 이긴 값 같은 건 없어요.
before: No victory payment on this cup.
after: I didn't stake anything on this cup.

before: Um, thank you earlier.
after: Um, thank you for earlier.

before: If you hear this voice, let's keep it.
after: If you can hear me like this, I'd like to keep this voice.

korean: 이긴 얘기만 하면 짧아요. 진 얘기도 해 볼까요?
before: Only victories is short. Defeats too?
after: Only telling victories makes it short. Shall I tell you about defeats, too?

before: Laughed my throat dry.
after: I've laughed my throat dry.

korean: 지금은 여기에 들릴 만큼만 말하고 싶어요.
before: Right now, just enough for here.
after: Right now, just loud enough for you.

korean: 크게 하려면 하려던 말이 더 안 나와요.
before: Trying louder makes the words harder.
after: Trying to speak louder makes it harder to find the words.

before: Next time, less hesitation.
after: Next time, I'll try not to hesitate so long.

before: Slow and long is fine, right?
after: It's fine if I take my time, right?

before: Thought I could go anywhere.
after: I thought I could go anywhere.

before: Choosing, I just keep staying here.
after: But when I try to choose, I just stay here.

korean: 지금 여기 있고 싶으면 그래도 돼요.
before: If you want here now, stay.
after: If you want to stay here now, stay.

korean: 아까부터 사람 더 부를 생각은 안 했네요.
before: No thought of calling more people lately.
after: Lately, I haven't thought of calling more people over.

before: Fixing my ears would make laughing hard too.
after: Trying to fix my ears would make it hard to laugh, too.

before: Then I'll look where you mentioned.
after: Then I'll look where you asked me to.

before: Cup shook.
after: The cup shook in my hands.

before: Down before a spill.
after: I'll put it down before I spill.

korean: 누가 시키는 게 없어서 더 낯설었어요.
before: More unfamiliar without anyone ordering me.
after: It felt stranger without anyone giving me orders.

before: Today, why I came to Torva.
after: Today I'll talk about why I came to Torva.

before: I don't want constant movement as escape.
after: I don't want to keep moving just to escape the feeling.

before: I want to learn whether I may be still.
after: I want to learn that I can stay still, too.

before: No rushing while I'm still.
after: You won't rush me while I'm still?

korean: 문은 조금 열고 손은 쉬어 볼게요.
before: Door ajar, hands resting.
after: I'll leave the door ajar and let my hands rest.

korean: 다음에도 저 보러 오게 해야 했으니까요.
before: Had to bring them back next time.
after: I had to make them come back next time.

before: Their affection pleased me.
after: I was glad they liked me.

before: Now there are things for just two.
after: Now there are things I want to share with just one person.

korean: 이번엔 목소리 키우지 않고 해 볼게요.
before: This time, without raising my voice.
after: This time, I won't raise my voice.

korean: 한 번 앉고 나니까 아까보다 말하기가 나아요.
before: Seated, words come easier than before.
after: Sitting here, I find the words more easily than before.

before: Even after buying freedom, frightened nights came.
after: Even after I bought my freedom, some nights frightened me.

korean: 웃으면서 말해도 한 번 더 물어봐 줘요.
before: Even smiling, ask me once more.
after: Even if I'm smiling, ask me once more.

before: Late getting to sleep, but deeply.
after: I fell asleep late, but slept deeply.

before: Next fear, I'll tell without hiding.
after: Next time I'm scared, I'll tell you instead of hiding it.

before: Laughing like this, with no audience.
after: I'm laughing like this, even without an audience.

before: Before I start coughing.
after: I'd better drink before I start coughing.

before: You heard I want rest, right?
after: You heard me say I want to rest, right?

korean: 그럼 내일은 좀 쉬고 나서 봐요.
before: Then tomorrow, after some rest.
after: Then tomorrow, after we have rested.

korean: 못 가면 이유를 듣고 다시 정해요.
before: Unable? Hear why and decide anew.
after: If one of us can't come, let's hear why and decide again.

korean: 지금 못 가는 날부터 세어 두지 않아도 되겠죠?
before: No counting absent days now, right?
after: We aren't counting the days I can't come now, right?

before: Accepted before I changed the subject.
after: You accepted before I could change the subject.

korean: 다른 사람이 들으면 다시 목이 막힐 것 같아요.
before: Others hearing might choke my words again.
after: If others were listening, the words might stick in my throat again.

before: A little hurt.
after: It did hurt a little.

before: Then I thought I was fine too.
after: At the time, I thought I was fine, too.

before: I feared scolding for changing words.
after: I was afraid you'd scold me for changing my answer.

korean: 아까 못 한 말은 지금 이어서 할게요.
before: What I couldn't say earlier, now.
after: I'd like to say now what I couldn't say earlier.

before: Enough laughter today.
after: I've laughed enough today.

korean: 가자고 부르면 괜히 또 웃게 되니까요.
before: Being called makes me smile again needlessly.
after: When they call me, I start smiling again without meaning to.

before: If dull, discuss it coming back.
after: If it's dull, we can talk about it on the way back.

korean: 잔을 치우면 가야 할 것 같으니 조금만 더 둬요.
before: Cleared cups feel like departure. Leave them longer.
after: Clearing the cups feels like leaving. Let's leave them a little longer.

before: Someone to leave with today.
after: Today there's someone to leave with.

before: I'll tell my pace on the way too.
after: I'll tell you if the pace is too much on the way, too.

before: Unknown still. Hands still.
after: We don't know what it is yet. Keep your hands back.

before: I won't pretend a lone discovery.
after: I won't pretend I discovered it alone.

before: Breath before praise.
after: Catch your breath before the praise.

before: Everyone fine? That's enough.
after: Everyone's all right? That's enough for me.

before: No audience doesn't mean careless work!
after: No audience doesn't mean we can be careless!

korean: 제가 앞에 서도 혼자 가진 않아요.
before: Even leading, not going alone.
after: Even if I lead, I won't go alone.

before: Different from arena stories.
after: This is different from arena stories.

before: No smiling claims you're fine!
after: No smiling and claiming you're fine!

before: I won't only wait for 'fine.'
after: I won't just wait for you to say you're fine.

before: Oh, wounded! Still standing!
after: Oh, I'm wounded! Still standing!

korean: 아픈 데 없다는 말은 못 하겠어요!
before: Can't claim nothing hurts!
after: I can't claim nothing hurts!

before: Asked before going quiet alone.
after: I asked before going quiet on my own.

before: Someone to meet after returning too.
after: There's someone to meet when I return, too.

korean: 빚 갚은 날 얘기를 해도 될까요?
before: May I tell repayment day?
after: May I tell you about the day I repaid it?

korean: 재밌을지는 아직 모르지만 가 보고 싶어요.
before: Don't know if fun. Still want to go.
after: I don't know if it'll be fun. I still want to go.

before: I said fine earlier. A little hurt.
after: I said I was fine earlier. It hurt a little.

before: Late, but I want to say it now.
after: It's late, but I want to say it now.

korean: 코트가 있으니 나는 좀 더 있을게.
before: I've my coat. I'll stay longer.
after: I've got my coat. I'll stay longer.

korean: 금방 옮길 수 있게 두고 싶어.
before: Want it easy to move.
after: I want it easy to move.

before: Clear passage, and it's fine.
after: Keep the passage clear, and it's fine.

before: More drying, then I'll wear it.
after: I'll let it dry more, then wear it.

korean: 이쪽은 비 안 맞아요. 옮겨 걸까요?
before: Dry here. Hang it over here?
after: It's dry here. Shall we hang it here?

korean: 소매 안쪽까지 마르면 다시 입을 거야.
before: Once the sleeve lining dries, back on.
after: Once the sleeve lining dries, I'll put it back on.

before: Wet footing. Slowly.
after: It's wet underfoot. Go slowly.

before: Folded again here.
after: It's creased here again.

korean: 이렇게 눌러 두면 덜 접힐 거야.
before: Press it like this. Less folding.
after: Press it like this. Fewer creases.

before: Can see who's coming outside.
after: I can see who is coming from outside.

before: Everyone would make here noisy too.
after: Everyone coming would make it noisy here, too.

korean: 여기 앉으니 바람이 등에 안 닿네.
before: Seated here, no wind on my back.
after: Sitting here keeps the wind off my back.

korean: 두 분 다 안쪽으로 모시면 더 편하겠네요.
before: Bring you both inside. Easier.
after: I'll bring you both inside. Easier.

before: Sometimes I like there.
after: Sometimes I like it there.

before: Caught my foot passing.
after: It caught my foot as I passed.

before: Shared a blanket in winter.
after: I shared a blanket in winter.

korean: 몸을 돌릴 때마다 조금 깨곤 했어.
before: Woke a little at every turn.
after: Woke a little whenever someone turned over.

before: Pull it, and your neighbor wakes.
after: Pull the blanket and your neighbor wakes.

korean: 응. 오늘은 나눠 덮을 만큼 춥지도 않아.
before: Yes. Not cold enough to share today.
after: Yes. It's not cold enough to need to share today.

before: Comfortable, pulled over my knees.
after: It's comfortable pulled over my knees.

before: Went for lodging permission in Harben.
after: I went to ask for lodging permission in Harben.

before: Knowing it, still go outside.
after: I know that. Still go outside.

before: Inside pocket. Must stay dry.
after: Inside pocket. It must stay dry.

korean: 계약증은 있어. 오늘은 천천히 정할 거야.
before: I have the certificate. Choosing slowly today.
after: I've got the certificate. Today I can take my time choosing.

korean: 오늘은 눈을 뜰 때 어깨가 덜 뻐근했어.
before: Less shoulder ache waking today.
after: My shoulders ached less when I woke today.

korean: 조금 먼저 일어났어요. 물도 반 잔 떠 놨어요.
before: Up a little earlier. Half a cup ready too.
after: I got up a little earlier. Poured half a cup for you, too.

before: Especially the alley's end.
after: Especially at the end of the alley.

before: I know cold.
after: I do feel the cold.

korean: 밖에 오래 서 있으면 발부터 아프더라.
before: Long standing outside hurts feet first.
after: Stand outside long enough, and your feet hurt first.

before: Chair close to the wall leaves room.
after: With the chair against the wall, there's room to pass.

before: Ask their story seated.
after: Ask about their story once they're seated.

korean: 의자 붙였으니 한 사람은 더 앉겠네.
before: Chairs close. Room for one more.
after: The chairs are close. There's room for one more.

before: I'll report the drier places afterward.
after: I'll tell you which stretches are dry afterward.

before: Then eat a little while waiting.
after: Then I can eat a little while waiting.

korean: 다음에는 내 접시부터 조금 먹을 거야.
before: Next time, some of my plate first.
after: Next time, I'll start on my food first.

before: Eyes closed here.
after: I'll close my eyes here.

before: Then I'll close my eyes easily.
after: Then I can close my eyes without worrying.

korean: 내일은 들어올 때 내가 먼저 볼게.
before: Tomorrow I'll look when you enter first.
after: Tomorrow I'll watch for you coming in.

before: Briefly outside too.
after: I'll step outside briefly, too.

before: Blind spots together.
after: Let's check the blind spots together.

before: A word when passing.
after: Say something when you pass.

before: I'll check for quiet around us further.
after: I'll listen a little longer for sounds around us.

before: Back home, inside rest today.
after: When we're home, I'll rest inside today.

before: Back home, eating without words.
after: Back home, let's eat without talking.

before: Movement needs another look.
after: Check again before moving them.

before: No rushing you upright.
after: I won't rush you to stand.

before: Let’s figure out how to leave together.
after: Let's figure out how to leave together.

before: This time, a little painful.
after: This time, it does hurt a little.

before: Hand won't fit well here.
after: My hand won't fit well here.

korean: 함께 볼 만큼은 기다릴 수 있어.
before: I can wait for a shared look.
after: I can wait until we look together.

before: Wait here if waiting.
after: If you're waiting, wait here.

before: A little Harben winter talk?
after: May I tell you a little about winter in Harben?

korean: 국까지 내 말의 편을 들 필요는 없는데요.
before: Even soup needn't take my side.
after: Even sharing soup need not mean taking my side.

before: I have ears while eating.
after: I can listen while I eat.

korean: 말 적게 하는 날에도 국은 내줄 수 있소.
before: Even quiet days allow soup offered.
after: I can offer soup even on quiet days.

korean: 사이가 풀릴 때까지 일도 쉬시는 게 낫겠어요.
before: Take work off until we're reconciled too.
after: Don't work until we've made up, either.

korean: 도울 손까지 우리 기분으로 미루지는 맙시다.
before: Let's not postpone helping hands for our moods.
after: Let's not put off helping others because of how we feel.

korean: 성표를 넣어도 도울 손까지 넣지는 않소.
before: Symbol tucked away. Helping hands stay out.
after: My symbol is tucked away. My hands are still free to help.

before: A convenient thought for me.
after: That was a convenient thought for me.

before: Words can rest while tea cools.
after: Let our words rest while the tea cools.

korean: 좋은 뜻으로 남의 귀를 정할 순 없지요.
before: Good intentions can't choose another's ears.
after: Good intentions can't decide what someone else wants to hear.

korean: 끝까지 듣고 내 말은 뒤에 놓겠소.
before: I'll hear you out. My words afterward.
after: I'll hear you out, then have my say.

before: Thought everyone welcomed help.
after: I thought everyone welcomed help.

before: Hurry, and I'll push it over again.
after: If I hurry, I'll push the bowl toward them again before asking.

before: Soup cools while waiting for debate.
after: Soup cools while we wait to debate.

korean: 배부터 채우고 나서도 기도는 할 수 있소.
before: We can still pray after we’ve eaten.
after: We can still pray after we've eaten.

before: Thank you. Out of the draft.
after: Thank you. Put it out of the draft.

korean: 수저 드는 데 신 이름을 시험하진 않소.
before: No test of divine names for lifting a spoon.
after: No one needs a test on the gods' names before lifting a spoon.

korean: 의자 하나 더 놓는 데 교리는 길지 않소.
before: One more chair needs little doctrine.
after: We need little doctrine to offer one more chair.

korean: 칭찬이라고 하려면 꽤 오래 웃는 법을 배웠소.
before: It took years learning to laugh before calling it praise.
after: It took me years to learn to laugh at it, and call it praise.

before: Asking whether I smiled from the start.
after: You're asking whether I smiled from the start.

korean: 웃게 된 말도 처음 들을 때는 달랐소.
before: Even words I laugh at sounded different first.
after: Even the words I laugh at now once sounded different.

before: Barracks suffice.
after: The barracks will do.

korean: 사람이 있으면 손을 모을 수는 있소.
before: With people, hands can still join.
after: Where there are people, we can still join our hands.

before: Want to pray? Find permitted space first?
after: If you want to pray, shall we find a permitted space first?

korean: 건물을 못 세운다고 마음까지 접지는 않소.
before: No building doesn't mean abandoning my heart.
after: Having no building does not mean abandoning what I believe.

before: Just leave passage.
after: Just leave room to pass.

korean: 지금 다 듣고 고개 끄덕일 필요는 없소.
before: No need to hear everything and nod now.
after: You need not hear everything and nod along now.

before: Slowly, like soup.
after: We can take it slowly, as with soup.

before: No profession for convenience.
after: Do not profess belief just for convenience.

korean: 그런 식탁이면 내 말도 너무 크지 않겠소.
before: At such a table, my voice won't loom too large.
after: At a table like that, I will not drown out the other voices.

korean: 아, 내가 대신 답할 일은 아니구려.
before: Ah, not mine to answer.
after: Ah, that is not my answer to give.

korean: 남의 겁을 내 농담감으로 키울 필요는 없소.
before: No need to grow another's fear for my jokes.
after: I need not make someone more afraid for the sake of a joke.

korean: 농담하는 손으로 남의 겁까지 흔들진 않겠소.
before: Joking hands mustn't shake another's fear too.
after: A joke should not make someone already frightened tremble more.

korean: 웃을 때 옆에 있었는지가 더 오래 남지요.
before: Who stayed beside the laughter lasts longer.
after: People remember who stayed beside them longer than the laughter.

before: Started too many things.
after: I started too many things.

korean: 웃고 넘기면 또 남의 몫이 되겠소.
before: Laugh it off, and someone else inherits it.
after: If I laugh it off, someone else is left with the work.

before: I recorded others' hands as my own.
after: I counted other people's help as if I had done it myself.

before: Who clears what laughter leaves?
after: Who finishes the work left behind by the laughter?

korean: 벌인 일은 농담보다 작은 것부터 끝내겠소.
before: I'll finish my undertakings, small tasks before jokes.
after: I will finish what I undertook. Small tasks before jokes.

before: Lateness means no smaller meal.
after: Arriving late should not mean a smaller meal.

before: Haven't heard their hunger's story.
after: We have not heard why they are hungry.

before: Simply want it warm.
after: I simply want their food to be warm.

before: Cover briefly against cooling.
after: Cover it for a moment so it will not cool.

korean: 굶은 입에 질문부터 채우고 싶진 않네요.
before: I don't want questions filling a hungry mouth first.
after: I do not want them answering questions before they can fill their hungry mouths.

before: Even answering mouths need soup and rest.
after: Even someone who owes an answer needs soup and rest.

before: First heard it coming down the mountain.
after: I first heard it as I came down the mountain.

korean: 지금 웃는 입으로 그때 아팠던 말도 할 수 있소.
before: Today's smiling mouth can tell yesterday's hurts too.
after: Now I can smile as I speak of what once hurt.

korean: 칭찬으로 듣기 전의 시간도 여기 놓아요.
before: Lay the years before praise here too.
after: Let us hear about the years before you could call it praise, too.

before: Thought I'd only set down the symbol.
after: I thought I was only setting down my holy symbol.

korean: 성표 옆에 놓은 십 년도 같이 봐 주시오.
before: See the ten years beside the symbol too.
after: Think of those ten years when you look at the symbol, too.

before: 'Nowhere to return' is wrong.
after: It is wrong to say I have nowhere to return to.

before: Yes. People here too.
after: Yes. There are people here, too.

before: Never heard their names.
after: I never heard their names.

korean: 이름을 몰라도 오늘 그분들을 위해 기도하겠소.
before: Unnamed, I still pray for them today.
after: Even without their names, I will pray for them today.

before: I don't know their names. Still, prayers for them.
after: I do not know their names. Still, I will pray for them.

before: I touched another's symbol too lightly.
after: I was too careless when I touched someone else's symbol.

before: Thought closeness allowed everything.
after: I thought being close meant I could do anything.

korean: 가까운 손이라 더 놀랐을 수도 있겠네요.
before: A familiar hand may startle more.
after: A familiar hand can startle someone even more.

korean: 좋은 뜻보다 그분이 싫었던 데부터 들어요.
before: Their dislike before your intentions.
after: Their discomfort comes before explaining your intentions.

korean: 내 성표를 놓는 손으로 남의 선도 지켜야겠소.
before: The hand laying my symbol must respect others' boundaries too.
after: The hand that holds my symbol must respect the boundaries of others, too.

korean: 오늘은 웃는 쪽으로 끝내지 않아도 돼요.
before: Today's needn't end in laughter.
after: Today's conversation need not end in laughter.

before: Then a little of the nights first.
after: Then I will tell a little of those nights first.

korean: 사제가 답 못 하는 밤도 잠깐은 받아 주시오.
before: Accept briefly a priest's unanswered nights too.
after: Allow a priest to speak of nights without answers, too.

korean: 흔들린 밤도 제 믿음 옆에 두고 말하겠소.
before: I'll speak of wavering nights beside my faith.
after: I will speak of my nights of doubt alongside my faith.

before: Keep mine too.
after: Keep a portion for me, too.

korean: 항상 국 끝을 보던 버릇이 있소.
before: A habit of finding the soup gone.
after: I am used to finding the soup has all gone.

before: Today, serving together.
after: Today, let us serve ourselves together.

before: An accustomed stomach still hungers.
after: Even a stomach used to waiting feels hunger.

korean: 돌보던 손도 수저 들 때는 같이 배고프오.
before: Helping hands hunger too when lifting spoons.
after: Even someone who helps others feels hungry when lifting a spoon.

korean: 남의 밥보다 내 밥이 늦을 이유는 없겠소.
before: No reason my meal follows everyone else's.
after: There is no reason my meal must come after everyone else has eaten.

korean: 국 떠 주던 손으로 내 그릇도 들어 볼게요.
before: The soup-serving hand can lift my bowl too.
after: The hand serving soup can lift my own bowl, too.

before: Without a priest's face.
after: Without having to look the part of a priest.

korean: 오늘은 대답을 만들어 주는 입도 쉬어 가고 싶소.
before: The answer-making mouth wants rest too.
after: Even someone always expected to answer wants a rest.

korean: 손을 편 동안은 남의 하루를 받아 들겠소.
before: With open hands, I'll receive another's day.
after: With my hands free, I will listen to your day.

korean: 내 말이 커서 그걸 덜 말했네요.
before: My loud words left that unsaid.
after: I talked so loudly about myself that I left her part unsaid.

before: I'd like the days you leaned on her too.
after: I'd like to hear about the days you leaned on her, too.

before: Her story too.
after: I will talk about her, too.

before: Awkward or not, I received too.
after: Awkward or not, there were days I accepted help.

korean: 받는 내 모습까지 모르는 건 아니오.
before: I know myself receiving as well.
after: I know what I am like when I receive help, too.

korean: 곁에서 도와준 사람 얘기도 하고 싶소.
before: I want to tell of those helping beside me too.
after: I want to speak of those who helped beside me, too.

korean: 누구든 돕겠소만, 믿음 얘기도 하고 싶소.
before: I'll help anyone. I want faith talk too.
after: I will help anyone. I still want to talk about faith.

korean: 다르게 믿어도 그 사람 말은 들어 봅시다.
before: Even different beliefs, hear their words.
after: Even if their beliefs differ, hear them out.

korean: 지친 사제도 오늘 그릇 셀 사람 수에 넣어 주시오.
before: Count the tired priest among today's bowls too.
after: Include the tired priest when you count the bowls today, too.

before: One thing finished first.
after: I will finish one thing first.

before: No smiling promises to do everything.
after: I will not smile and promise to do everything.

before: I'll ask for missing hands.
after: I will ask for help where we are short of hands.

before: Yes, the existing work finished first.
after: Yes, but let us finish the work already begun first.

korean: 벌인 일 끝에 누구 손이 남을지부터 세겠소.
before: First count whose hands remain when it's done.
after: First count who will still be working when the task is done.

korean: 오늘 벌일 말은 마칠 손을 세고 나서 하겠소.
before: Today I'll count finishing hands before announcing beginnings.
after: Today I will count who can finish the work before announcing new tasks.

before: Especially doubtful nights.
after: Especially on nights of doubt.

before: Even a priest's answerless face is welcome?
after: Even a priest without answers is welcome?

korean: 확신 오기 전 밤이 조금 길어서요.
before: The night before certainty runs long.
after: The night is long when you are waiting for certainty.

korean: 확신이 오기 전에도 밤은 혼자 길어지더군요.
before: Even before certainty, nights lengthen alone.
after: And longer alone, with nothing certain yet.

korean: 답이 없는 밤에도 부를 사람이 생겼네요.
before: Now there's someone to call on unanswered nights.
after: Now I have someone to call on nights without answers.

korean: 분쟁을 피하려고 늘 내 성표만 숨겨야 하면 서운하오.
before: Always only my symbol hidden for peace would hurt.
after: It would hurt if keeping the peace always meant hiding only my symbol.

korean: 같은 그릇을 써도 성표까지 바꿀 건 없겠소.
before: Shared bowls needn't change symbols.
after: Sharing food need not change what we believe.

korean: 서로 밀어내지 말고 내 성표도 꺼내겠소.
before: Without pushing others out, mine comes out too.
after: I can show my symbol without pushing others aside.

korean: 앉겠다는 첫말이 국보다 늦게 들렸나 보오.
before: My 'sit first' arrived later than the soup, apparently.
after: My wish to sit first seems to have reached you later than the soup.

korean: 밥 주는 손만 기다린 건 아니었구려.
before: Not only waiting for serving hands.
after: You were not just waiting for someone to serve.

before: Then tea-pouring sounds first.
after: Then let us listen to the tea being poured first.

before: Quiet is my face today too.
after: Being quiet is part of who I am today, too.

korean: 농담은 안 나와도 옆에 있을 마음은 있소.
before: No joke, but still a wish to stay beside you.
after: I have no joke, but I still want to stay beside you.

korean: 농담 쉬는 시간에도 식탁 소리는 남네요.
before: Even jokes resting leave table sounds.
after: Even when the jokes rest, we can hear the sounds at the table.

before: Finished, I see this place.
after: Now the prayer is over, I can see this place again.

korean: 다 아는 얼굴로 오지 않아도 되겠소.
before: No need for an all-knowing face.
after: I need not pretend to know everything.

korean: 답 없는 기도 끝에도 돌아올 식탁은 있소.
before: Even unanswered prayer has a table to return to.
after: Even after a prayer without an answer, I have a table to return to.

korean: 같이 꺼낼 그릇까지 없애면 좀 허전하겠소.
before: Removing even bowls to bring out together feels empty.
after: It feels empty if you take away even the bowls we could bring out together.

korean: 그럼 밥 얘기 전에 반갑다고 하겠소.
before: Before food, I'll say I'm glad.
after: Before serving food, I will say I am glad to see you.

korean: 돌아오며 떠올린 자리에 오늘도 사람이 있소.
before: Again, someone fills the place I imagined returning to.
after: Again today, someone is waiting in the place I hoped to return to.

before: Today, leave having eaten together.
after: Today, let us eat together before leaving.

before: Different gods to lean on are fine.
after: It is all right to turn to different gods.

before: Descend beside me, and voices reach.
after: Come down beside me, where we can hear each other.

before: Not a priest hearing only others' doubts.
after: I am not a priest who hears only the doubts of others.

before: Finder's keen eyes.
after: The finder has a keen eye.

before: Record the hands sharing the sight too.
after: Record who saw it together, too.

korean: 모르는 데까지 기도 말로 채우진 않소.
before: No prayers filling gaps of ignorance.
after: Do not fill the gaps in what we know with prayers.

korean: 나중에 밥 먹으며 이 얘기도 해요.
before: This story over food later too.
after: Let us hear this story again over food later.

korean: 다 해내겠단 말은 좀 아껴 둘게요.
before: I'll spare promises to do everything.
after: I will refrain from promising to do everything.

before: Now call the workers by name.
after: Now call those who did the work by name.

korean: 오늘 고맙다는 말은 기도 뒤로 안 미룰게요.
before: Thanks won't wait behind prayer today.
after: Today I will say thank you before praying.

before: No opponent for long sermons.
after: This is no opponent for long sermons.

korean: 내가 벌린 말보다 할 수 있는 손부터요.
before: Available hands before my grand words.
after: Let us count who can help before listening to my grand words.

korean: 답을 아는 얼굴로만 서 있진 않을게요.
before: I won't stand only wearing an answer's face.
after: I will not pretend to have all the answers.

before: Helping hands received help today too.
after: Those who help others received help today, too.

korean: 괜찮다는 말 뒤도 한 번 더 들어요.
before: Hear beyond 'fine' once more.
after: Hear more than just 'I am fine' once more.

korean: 그 사람 대답부터 내 말보다 앞에 두오.
before: Their answer before my words.
after: Their answer comes before my words.

before: Helping hands available? Borrow them together.
after: Is anyone able to help? Let us ask them together.

korean: 답을 못 받아도 곁을 비우지는 않겠소.
before: No answer won't make me leave their side.
after: No answer will make me leave their side.

before: Today my bowl needs attention too.
after: Today I need some care, too.

before: Hands caring for others rest briefly.
after: These hands that care for others will rest a moment.

korean: 기도 아닌 말로 한 잔쯤 해도 되지요.
before: A cup can have words besides prayer.
after: We can share words besides prayer over a cup.

before: People before spoons counted.
after: Count people before spoons.

before: Barracks soup after returning.
after: There will be soup at the barracks when we return.

korean: 답을 못 찾은 날도 이쪽으로 돌아오겠소.
before: Answerless days bring me back here too.
after: Even on days without answers, I return here.

korean: 남겨진 일을 웃음 뒤에 놓진 않을게요.
before: Unfinished duties won't hide behind smiles.
after: I will not hide unfinished duties behind a smile.

korean: 기도의 답은 몰라도 돌아갈 곁은 있소.
before: Prayer's answer unknown, but there's company to return to.
after: I do not know the answer to my prayer, but I have someone to return to.

korean: 실패한 사제 얼굴도 오늘은 숨기지 않겠소.
before: Today I won't hide a failed priest's face either.
after: Today I will not hide from you even when I feel I have failed as a priest.

before: I decided you'd accept first.
after: I assumed you would accept before I asked.

before: Years before I heard it as praise.
after: It took years before I could hear it as praise.

korean: 그 십 년도 한번 말해 보고 싶네요.
before: I'd like to tell those ten years too.
after: I would like to tell you about those ten years, too.

before: Some nights wavered.
after: There were nights when my faith wavered.

korean: 모자란 손은 남의 것처럼 쓰지 않고요.
before: No treating missing hands as mine to command.
after: I will not treat anyone available to help as mine to command.

before: Again, 'everything' ran ahead of me.
after: Again, my promise to do 'everything' ran ahead of me.

before: Ask whose hands will undertake it first again.
after: Let us ask again who will actually do the work first.

korean: 밥 주러 오지 않아도 자리가 있네요.
before: A place even without serving food.
after: There is a place for me even when I serve no food.

before: I said quiet days are my face too.
after: I said quiet days were part of who I am, too.

korean: 그 말은 다시 약속으로 남겨 둘래요.
before: I'll leave that as a promise again.
after: I will make that promise again.

before: Looks tell you all my strength?
after: Can you tell how much strength I have just by looking?

before: Just trip hazards out.
after: Just clear anything we could trip on.

before: Here is final.
after: This is where it'll stay.

before: Hands washed before drinking.
after: I'll wash my hands before drinking.

before: Sand in my hands.
after: There's sand in my hands.

before: Won't grip again like this.
after: I won't grip anything again like this.

before: Then against the wall.
after: Then put it against the wall.

before: This hand will do.
after: I can carry it in this hand.

before: With that, I can reach alone.
after: With that, I can see and reach it myself.

before: Clean now, less slipping next time.
after: Clean it now, and it won't slip next time.

before: Slip, and the wrist hurts first.
after: If it slips, your wrist takes the strain first.

korean: 끝부분만 잡아. 손 가까이는 닦아야 해.
before: Just the end. Must clean near the handgrip.
after: Just hold the end. I need to clean near the grip.

before: Cleaning before injury.
after: I'll clean it before I get hurt.

korean: 다 들면 길 막힐 때 손을 못 써.
before: Everything leaves no free hand if blocked.
after: If I take everything, I have no hand free when something blocks us.

before: Then water and route for me.
after: Then I'll handle the water and the route.

korean: 그릇만 옮기면 이쪽에 앉을 수 있어.
before: Move your bowl, and room here.
after: Move your bowl and there's room here.

korean: 직접 치워 보게 하면 덜 무서워할 텐데요.
before: Removing it herself would ease the fear.
after: Removing it herself would help her get over the fear.

before: Dust swept outside.
after: I've swept the dust outside.

before: Stretch your feet. Room below.
after: Stretch your legs. There's room under the table.

before: Open hands feel better.
after: My hands feel better open.

before: Numbers in the mines.
after: In the mines, we had numbers.

before: Conscripted to suppress Drum.
after: I was conscripted to suppress the revolt in Drum.

before: Miners inside.
after: The miners were inside.

before: No. Something scorched.
after: No. Something is scorched.

before: Wind this way would help.
after: A breeze this way would help.

before: Familiar can still be hateful.
after: You can know a smell and still hate it.

before: Yes. Should clear meanwhile.
after: Yes. The smell should clear meanwhile.

korean: 들기 전에 바퀴부터 보는 버릇이 남았어.
before: Still check wheels before lifting.
after: Still check the wheels before lifting.

before: Came after hearing of contract certificates.
after: I came after hearing about contract certificates.

before: Choose again, and I'd cross.
after: If I had to choose again, I'd cross over.

before: Keep thinking how it must've felt.
after: I keep thinking of how it must have felt.

before: Today I'll ask help too.
after: Today I'll ask for help, too.

before: Hands slip undoing straps.
after: My hands slip when I undo the straps.

before: Today I want your grip.
after: Today I want you to hold it with me.

before: Stay there. Knot visible now.
after: Stay there. I can see the knot now.

before: Spoons together today.
after: Today we'll start eating together.

before: Didn't hurt here for a while.
after: It hadn't hurt here for a while.

before: Speak if it hurts tomorrow too.
after: Tell me if it still hurts tomorrow.

before: Hurts again with each use.
after: It hurts again every time I use it.

before: These fingers need slow stretching.
after: I need to stretch these fingers slowly.

before: Especially hard to see beneath packs.
after: It's especially hard to see under the packs.

before: I'll turn at a call. Use it.
after: I'll turn when you call. Call me.

before: Rest gives mine now.
after: Rest gives me peace of mind now.

korean: 손이 비면 나도 좀 덜 움직이겠지.
before: Empty hands might slow me too.
after: Having nothing to carry might help me slow down, too.

before: Yours while I'm gone, then.
after: Then look after mine while I'm gone, too.

before: First, what's happening?
after: Let's see what's happening first.

korean: 매번 할 수 있는 건 아니야.
before: Can't every time.
after: Can't do it every time.

before: Same road. Could be in yours.
after: We walked the same road. You could have one in yours.

before: Stop, and it comes out immediately.
after: Stop and you can take it out at once.

before: Less knocking my knees here.
after: I don't keep knocking my knees here.

korean: 의자만 조금 당기면 발이 더 편해.
before: Chair closer, easier feet.
after: Pull the chair closer. More comfortable for your feet.

before: Today, both rest.
after: Today we both rest.

before: I meant shared rest today.
after: I meant we should both rest today.

before: Today's pack journey ends here. Enough.
after: I've finished carrying today's pack. Enough.

before: Hold briefly. Shared step.
after: Hold a moment. We step together.

korean: 난 옆에서 길 안 막히게 서 있을게.
before: I'll stand beside, passage clear.
after: I'll stand beside you and keep the passage clear.

before: A word when passing.
after: Say something when you pass.

korean: 이번엔 네가 물병 좀 잡아 줘.
before: Your grip on the bottle this time.
after: Your turn to hold the bottle.

before: Breath, then shared walk.
after: Catch your breath, then we walk together.

korean: 나도 긴장돼. 가기 전에 숨 좀 고르자.
before: Nervous too. Breath before going.
after: Nervous too. Take a breath before going.

korean: 이제 손 놓으니까 팔이 좀 떨리네.
before: Hands free now. Arm shaking a little.
after: Hands free now. My arm is shaking a little.

before: Stiff hands stretched first.
after: I'll stretch my stiff hands first.

before: Pale face.
after: Your face is pale.

korean: 움직일 수 있으면 손을 보여 줘.
before: Movement? Show a hand.
after: Can you move? Show me your hand.

korean: 여기 있어. 네 목소리 듣고 있어.
before: Here. Hearing your voice.
after: I'm here. I can hear your voice.

before: Wait. Strange grip strength.
after: Wait. My grip feels wrong.

before: I'll check which side before going.
after: I'll check which side hurts before going.

before: Rest before asking if I'm fine.
after: I'll rest before trying to say I'm fine.

korean: 깨면 내 물부터 한 잔 마실게.
before: When I wake up, I will have some water first.
after: When I wake up, I'll have some water first.

before: Gap before pulling.
after: Check the gap before pulling.

korean: 이제 물은 여유 있게 마셔도 되겠네.
before: Now water without rationing.
after: Now we can drink water without rationing it.

korean: 잡을 데 없으면 내 팔 잡아.
before: No hold? My arm.
after: Nothing to hold? Take my arm.

before: Out together, then the next task.
after: Out together. Then we think of the next task.

before: Today's work, you may tell.
after: You can tell me about today's work.

before: I'll see only if I can do it.
after: I'll just see if I can do it.

before: Just tell the destination.
after: Just tell me the destination.

before: Mine prepared here.
after: My own load is ready here.

korean: 그 말은 네 앞에서 하고 싶었어.
before: Wanted those words before you.
after: Wanted to say that to you.

before: I'll speak immediately if struggling too.
after: I'll speak up right away if I'm struggling, too.

before: Packs down. Both seated.
after: Packs down. We both sit.

before: Sorting once we rise.
after: We can sort them when we get up.

before: My hand keeps grabbing here.
after: I keep reaching for the charm.

korean: 마개 하나가 뻑뻑해도 제 물병은 제가 챙길게요.
before: One stiff stopper does not mean I cannot mind my own bottle.
after: I can still take care of my own bottle, even if the stopper is stiff.

before: I won't omit it because it's my hand.
after: I won't neglect it just because it is my own hand.

korean: 제가 전할지 말지 정하고 싶은 얘기도 있어요.
before: Some stories need my own decision whether to share.
after: There are stories I want to decide for myself whether to share.

before: It keeps tipping over when I stand it up.
after: It keeps tipping over and rolling away when I stand it up.

korean: 손을 멈추면 말을 또 삼킬까 봐 식탁을 문지르고 있었어요.
before: I feared that keeping my hands still would make me swallow my words again.
after: I kept rubbing the table, afraid I would swallow my words again if my hands stopped.

korean: 첫 장 대신 오늘 적은 것부터 봐요.
before: Today's notes instead of the first page.
after: Let's look at today's notes instead of the first page.

before: I asked too many questions just to satisfy my curiosity, did I not?
after: I have asked so much about what interests me, have I not?

korean: 손이 먼저 가방으로 갔네요. 펜이 없는 줄 알고 잠깐 놀랐어요.
before: My hand went to my bag first. Not finding the pen startled me for a moment.
after: My hand went to my bag first. For a moment, I thought my pen was missing.

korean: 기록하기 전에 같이 한 번 더 살펴봐요.
before: Before recording, another shared look.
after: Let us look together once more before recording it.

korean: 끝났다는 걸 적으려니 아직 손이 떨리네요.
before: My hand still trembles recording the end.
after: My hand still trembles as I try to record that it is over.

korean: 잘 버티시니까 이 정도 바람은 그냥 걸어도 되죠?
before: You're tough. This wind needs no shelter.
after: You're tough. You can walk in this wind without shelter, right?

korean: 답을 못 받아도 곁을 비우지는 않겠소.
before: No answer will make me leave their side.
after: Even if they do not answer, I will not leave their side.

before: Now my hand rests.
after: Now I'll let my hand rest.

before: My hand can reach.
after: I can reach you.

before: Bear it a little. You'll warm up. I always do.
after: Bear it a little. You'll warm up. I do, too.

korean: 오늘은 대답을 만들어 주는 입도 쉬어 가고 싶소.

after: Even the person giving answers wants a rest.
